name: Model-visible equals logged session log
what: Everything a model sees is reconstructable from one append-only per-session event log, so any request, retry, tool outcome, approval or compaction can be audited or replayed after the fact.
how: SessionEventMap with 60 known event types, a seq/time envelope and lossless JSON; deriveMessages() projects model history from the log; AGENTS.md makes "model-visible iff logged" a standing rule (a new model-visible input needs a new event type); assistant/message embeds the exact timed stream; log-only events (request/header, approval/*, llm/retry) never become messages.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane streams runs as SSE events (apps/Model Plane/docs/sse-event-taxonomy.md) with no request-level durable event; a rule that every model-visible input has a durable event would give Verevon replayable runs, but the log has to be ZDR-aware (redact or expire at the persist boundary).
notes: The log stores full prompts, tool schemas and tool output on local disk for a single operator. Verevon must reconcile this with Zero-Data-Retention and tenant isolation. Claude Code transcripts and Codex rollouts log similar data but do not enforce the invariant as a repository rule.

name: Request header snapshots with effective config and full tool catalog
what: Each model request is preceded by a logged header recording provider, model, reasoning effort, temperature, max tokens, which of those the adapter defaulted, and the complete tool schema list; a new header is appended only when something changed.
how: "request/header" event {header: EpochHeader{config, adapterDefaults, tools}, reason: initial|resume|change|series, startsSeries}; callConfigEquals decides whether a proposed config is a real change; adapterDefaults flags fields materialised by the exact adapter rather than proposed by the caller; inspectRequestPrompt() reconstructs per-request state for the UI.
verevonRelevance: Verevon shows model and tokens only in the per-message Details popover (ChatMessages.tsx ReasoningPopover); a header event per run would let the Trace panel answer which model, effort and tool list produced an answer.

name: Route context metadata record (context window, system-prompt update mode)
what: A separate log-only record captures the routed model context window and whether the route accepts in-history system-prompt updates, written only when the route or capacity changes.
how: "request/context" event RequestContext{provider, model, contextWindow, systemPromptUpdate}; Session folds it incrementally (contextFold); the token-meter contextPressure projection reads contextWindow for the occupancy percentage.
verevonRelevance: Makes a context meter correct per model; Verevon ContextWindowPanel measures against an assembly budget, not the model window (ChatPanels.tsx:606-640).

name: System prompt as a logged, diffable surface node
what: The system prompt and later in-history updates are stored as system/message events, so the Trajectory view shows the exact prompt each request used and flags system, tools or system-and-tools changes between requests.
how: system/message surface node 0 plus positional replacements; inspectSystemPrompt and inspectRequestPrompt compute RequestPromptChange{kind: initial|system|tools|system-and-tools, previous}; Trajectory request-header rows and the System prompt and Tools tabs render it; compaction restores the last nonempty system prompt.
verevonRelevance: Per-request prompt and tool-schema diffs are rare in chat products and would help debug Model Plane prompt assembly; Model Plane GetContextAssembly returns segments but no per-request diff.
notes: Chat hides system-prompt and ordinary context rows in every work-details mode; they are inspectable only in Trajectory.

name: Trajectory ledger (turn/step/request event table)
what: A second conversation view beside Chat lists User, Assistant, Tool, nested Subtool and compaction records grouped by turn and step with request numbers and cumulative usage, plus search, fold-all controls and a record inspector; long histories are virtualised and open at the tail.
how: ui-trajectory registers a "trajectory" target on the ui-conversation event assembler (ConversationNodeDefinition per record kind); TrajectoryTable.tsx; 50-node anchored window with older pages loaded on demand; @tanstack/react-virtual; follows the tail until the user scrolls up; toolbar search and Turns/Calls fold toggles.
verevonRelevance: Verevon TracePanel lists event labels and times (ChatPanels.tsx:1410-1470) and StepsPanel keeps Technical activity collapsed; a record-level ledger with tokens, duration, input and output per step is the larger gap.
notes: Ships in the default Web bundle (not experimental). TrajectoryTable.tsx is about 3,500 lines. Selection is local to the view with no deep links (README limitation).

name: Trajectory timing overview with TTFT versus decode
what: A fixed timeline above the ledger draws each record real start and duration; assistant spans split time-to-first-token from decoding, with hover details, drag-to-focus an interval, wheel zoom and right-drag pan.
how: TrajectoryTimeline.tsx (Chrome-Network-style overview) and timeline.ts project recorded timing; TTFT is step start to first token including earlier retry attempts; throughput needs recorded usage; the toolbar toggles actual duration versus equal-width blocks; in-flight records show only a start marker.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Details popover splits Model time and System time from gateway turn_timing (ChatMessages.tsx ReasoningPopover); a per-step timeline would show where TTFT and tool latency go.

name: Honest timing: unavailable, never invented
what: When timing inputs are missing (step start not loaded, no first token, no usage, request still running) the UI says unavailable or shows only a start marker instead of estimating.
how: Locale keys timing.notAvailable, stepStartUnavailable, firstTokenUnavailable, usageUnavailable, outputTokensUnavailable, durationTooShort; a timing.source field distinguishes session timestamps from request timing; README states in-flight rows show a start marker without inventing elapsed time.
verevonRelevance: A cheap honesty rule for Verevon latency and cost fields (it already shows subscription turns as included instead of a placeholder zero, ChatMessages.tsx ReasoningPopover).

name: Trajectory record inspector with 13 tabs
what: Selecting a record opens an inspector with Summary, Preview, Raw, Source, Payload, Result, Schema, Timing, Diff, System prompt, Tools, Options and Usage tabs; run_code calls get numbered highlighted source with a toggle to the original JSON arguments.
how: Tab keys tab.summary through tab.usage; Schema shows the tool JSON schema, Options the request options JSON, Source the message source JSON; code-program.ts picks TypeScript or Python highlighting only from an unambiguous schema hint; images share the conversation per-session URL cache.
verevonRelevance: A Schema/Payload/Result/Options inspector per tool call would let Verevon users and support verify Model Plane tool calls; the current tools tab lists names only (ChatMessages.tsx ReasoningPopover).

name: Chat-to-Trajectory deep link on a tool call
what: Each tool card in Chat gets an Inspect action that opens the Trajectory view focused on that exact call.
how: ui-conversation apply.ts builds inspectCall(callId) only while a view target declares toolCallFocus; Trajectory declares toolCallFocus as callId => callId; TrajectoryView scrolls to the node containing the call id; ui-tool passes inspect through ToolCallTree.
verevonRelevance: Cheap link between a friendly chat card and its raw record; the Verevon shared/chat-nodes registry could carry a focus key the same way.

name: Message provenance vocabulary (source kind plus context form)
what: Every message and injected context declares who produced it (user, model, tool, system-prompt, or a plugin kind such as goal, schedule, webhook, subagent-settled) and what it is (instructions, catalog, snapshot, notice, relay, recall), so UIs can label injected context instead of showing it as user text.
how: MessageSourceMap is a merge-extensible sum type; ContextForm is a semantic union with form-specific required fields (notice needs a summary capped at 120 characters, snapshot needs named sections); Trajectory Source tab shows plugin-named and goal-round labels.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane injects memory, retrieval and system context into runs; a typed source plus form on each injected block would give Chat an honest why-is-this-in-context row (cf. memory_recall in the SSE taxonomy).

name: Non-human turn trigger attribution
what: When a turn starts from something other than the user (goal continuation, schedule, webhook or GitHub event, background job, subagent result, team message, plugin) Chat shows a labelled bordered notice stating that this notification triggered the response.
how: turnTriggerDetails maps source.kind (goal, agent-message, team-message, subagent-settled, webhook with provider github, schedule, tool-jobs, plugin) to a locale title key and icon; TurnTriggerNodeView renders it; trigger rows stay visible while ordinary context rows are hidden.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agents run scheduled and event-driven work (ScheduledRunsPanel, AgentRunConsole); labelling why each autonomous turn started supports audit and trust.

name: In-line context change rows (instructions, catalog, recall, supersession)
what: Context injected mid-conversation is summarised in the transcript: workspace instruction files loaded, added, updated or removed; replacement catalogs with an overflow count; messages relayed from another session; session recall with kept and omitted counts and a truncated flag; and a note when a snapshot supersedes earlier ones.
how: ContextForm renderers in ui-chat (ContextBody, ContextInjectionRow) with locale keys message.context.*; ordinary context rows are hidden in Chat in all work-details modes while tool-added and tool-removed rows stay visible; Trajectory keeps everything.
verevonRelevance: Maps onto Verevon memory_recall and retrieval_notice SSE events; the kept/omitted/truncated counts are a good honesty pattern for retrieval.
notes: Locale strings and README read; renderer internals were not traced.

name: Per-turn usage panel with exact buckets and all-or-nothing accounting
what: A completed turn shows an expandable Usage row with provider/model, cache hit %, uncached input, cached input, cache write, output and reasoning tokens; if any attempt lacks exact usage the row is hidden instead of showing a partial total.
how: deriveTurnTokenUsage(events) folds per-attempt usage and emits an aggregate only when every attempt reports that field; TurnUsagePanel dialog; TokenUsage carries inputTokens, outputTokens, totalTokens, cacheRead/WriteTokens and reasoningTokens; row hidden when the loaded window lacks turn/start.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Details popover shows input/output tokens and USD but not cache read/write or reasoning tokens; cache read appears only inside the collapsed technical disclosure (ChatPanels.tsx:926-940).

name: Session statistics pills from durable whole-log projections
what: Beneath the composer two pills show turns and steps with output speed (dialog: LLM time, tool time, average TTFT) and total tokens with cache hit; the figures survive paging, reloads and compaction because they come from whole-log projections.
how: session-stats projection unit (turns, steps, llmMs, toolMs, ttftMs/ttftSteps, decodeMs/decodeTokens) plus token-meter tokenUsage; StatsPills.tsx falls back to a window fold with identical field names; the pills are conversation.composer.dock entries replaceable by id; an e2e test pins behaviour under paged history.
verevonRelevance: Verevon metrics are per message; a session-level aggregate that is independent of paging needs a projection in Application Plane or Model Plane rather than client-side folds.

name: Cache-hit percentage that never rounds a partial hit to 100%
what: Cache-hit percentages use exact integer arithmetic and add decimal places (99.9, 99.99) rather than showing 100% when any prompt tokens missed the cache.
how: formatCacheHitPercent(cacheRead, promptTokens, decimals) computes rounded units by binary search over integer thresholds, returns 100 only when missed tokens are zero, otherwise extends precision until the value is below 100.
verevonRelevance: Small copyable honesty rule for Verevon cache and budget percentages (format-usd.ts exists for money; no equivalent for ratios was found).

name: Context occupancy ring with system, tools and messages breakdown
what: A ring and percentage below the composer shows how much of the model context window is used; clicking opens a breakdown into system prompt, tool definitions and messages.
how: contextOccupancy() divides projectedTokens (fallback pressureTokens) by the request/context window, capped at 100; the token-meter contextBreakdown projection supplies heuristic systemTokens, toolsTokens and messageTokens; the button stays hidden until usage and capacity are both known; covered by context-meter.e2e.ts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon ContextWindowPanel already itemises memories, sources and history against an assembly budget (ChatPanels.tsx:606), richer for retrieval; missing are the model-window percentage and the system/tool-schema split.
notes: Claude Code and Cursor have similar context meters; the log-derived projections are the differentiator.

name: Replay-aware token meter with provider-usage anchoring
what: Context pressure is computed deterministically from the durable log with no model call; provider-reported usage is reused only when the request envelope is identical, otherwise the request is estimated, and the docs say the figure is a reference, not billing.
how: TokenMeter fold with a measurement anchor; pressureTokens versus projectedTokens; fixed 4-characters-per-token heuristic plus adapter-declared image pricing; three projection units (tokenUsage, contextPressure, contextBreakdown); state version 5 invalidates checkpoints.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane cost and budget accounting could reuse the rule of anchoring on provider usage only when the envelope matches, so estimates do not drift.
notes: The heuristic underprices CJK text and JSON schemas (README says so). It is a token meter, not a currency meter.

name: Non-destructive compaction marker with counts and expandable summary
what: Compaction does not replace transcript rows; a marker states how many items and tokens were condensed and expands to the summary text, and compaction model requests appear as their own ledger rows between turns.
how: CompactionItem uses shadowedItemCount and shadowedTokenCount plus the cited summary node; Trajectory shows a standalone compaction request under Between turns and numbered compaction inside its turn; compaction/start..end bracket with lock; manual /compact command.
verevonRelevance: Verevon users should be told when history is condensed and be able to read the summary; condensed counts avoid silent context loss.

name: Durable, visible retry of failed model requests
what: Scheduled retries are logged before the wait, chat shows a waiting-to-retry status with attempt count and seconds, Trajectory keeps retry counts and the last attempt error after recovery, and docs state each retry is another billed request.
how: llm-retry appends llm/retry {retry id, provider, mode, policy key, failure, delay} then llm/retry-started; Retry-After from the provider replaces local backoff when in bounds; re-runs the failed step in the same open turn; nothing reaches the model.
verevonRelevance: Verevon stream retries are mostly invisible; a labelled retry state with delay and reason matches its truthfulness rules.

name: Turn end reasons and cancellation causes
what: Every turn ends with a typed reason (completed, aborted with a cause, blocked, error with structured failure, max-tokens, crash-interrupted, forked) and cancellations record who caused them (user, parent agent, hook, disposal).
how: TurnEndReasonMap and AgentCancelCause in session types; crash recovery appends turn/end "interrupted" for orphaned turns on resume or cold read; the abort signal reason is copied so stacks stay out of the log.
verevonRelevance: Verevon records cancellation receipts in TracePanel (ChatPanels.tsx:70); a closed vocabulary of end reasons and causes would sharpen audit.

name: Stable error codes with cause-chain rendering and localized failure rows
what: Failures carry stable machine codes (RATE_LIMIT, QUOTA, ACCOUNT_QUOTA, CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED, EMPTY_RESPONSE, INVALID_CREDENTIAL, MISSING_CREDENTIAL, AUTH, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT) and the UI renders localized, actionable rows; empty completions are treated as failures rather than silent ends.
how: HarnessError(code, cause) base; errorChain() renders full cause chains for diagnostics only (never parsed); classifiers for context-overflow and quota wording; adapters map HTTP statuses to codes; Chat shows a red-dot row per terminal failure and a quota-specific notice instead of the provider message.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already types errors as { error: { code, message, details } } envelopes; the EMPTY_RESPONSE rule and the code-versus-message split are worth checking in Model Plane adapters.

name: Honest tool-outcome uncertainty after failures
what: When a step fails or is cancelled, unanswered tool calls receive explicit error results (outcome unknown, not started, aborted before dispatch) and the model is told to retry only read-only or idempotent work and to check external state otherwise.
how: The agent loop records TOOL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN for a call with a start record but no result, TOOL_NOT_STARTED for a request without a call record, and synthetic tool/call plus ABORTED_BEFORE_DISPATCH pairs after cancellation; results stay in history until compaction.
verevonRelevance: Important for Verevon agents with external effects (browser actions, provider actions): an explicit unknown-outcome state prevents double-sending or false success claims.

name: Output-token limit notice with continue hint
what: When a step ends on its output-token ceiling, Chat shows an amber row stating the reply was cut off, that earlier output is preserved, and that sending "continue" resumes.
how: turn/end reason max-tokens (also set if a plugin continued the turn); turn-max-tokens node; amber dot; locale message.maxTokens and message.maxTokens.hint; a recorded SDK scenario and a web expected-output test cover the notice.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has continue-generation controllers (use-chat-controller.continue-generation.test.ts); the explicit notice wording is the extra.
notes: snapshots/sdk/max-tokens-continue is a directory; its scenario was seen in a listing and not opened.

name: Tool cards with a preparing stage and truncation honesty
what: A tool call is visible as soon as its name streams (one non-expandable row with icon and title), shows the file path and decoded size while arguments stream, then the result; capped search results carry a truncated flag so a partial result is never shown as complete, and a missing exit marker never establishes success.
how: tool.call.toolview keyed slot with explicit preparing, start and result props; lazy args reader; presentationMeta carries truncated and total for grep/glob; shell rows ending in a spill notice use generic expandable output; terminal cards for foreground bash and persistent shells.
verevonRelevance: Verevon shared/chat-nodes/tool-presentation.ts already exists; preparing rows and truncated flags are the checklist to compare against.

name: Replayable tool presentation metadata (two presentation layers)
what: Tool UI cards are pure functions of recorded arguments and persisted result metadata so history re-renders identically; host render intents (generic, terminal, diff, read, search, web) serve non-web clients while the Web client derives cards from raw events.
how: output.presentationMeta(args, value) is persisted on tool/result meta; presentCall and presentResult must be pure (no I/O, no clock) because they run on live streams and on log replay; Web registers wire tool names into tool.call.toolview and never consumes presentCall or presentResult.
verevonRelevance: Already studied by Verevon (claude-hermes-deepseek.md 13.2); the added detail is the explicit two-layer split and that results carry bounded structured meta.
notes: The prior Verevon analysis says never persist the view; this checkout persists meta on tool/result but derives views at render, which is consistent with that rule.

name: Output spill notices point to the full result
what: Oversized tool output is shown as a head and tail preview with a notice giving omitted bytes and the path of the full result, which the model can read with offset or grep; images stay in attachment storage with their paths recorded.
how: spill-policy with maxInlineTokens 12500 in the base profile; spill-local stores files private to the session; the notice text is model-visible and the UI recognises it for expandable output.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane tool-result truncation should leave a retrievable artifact and tell both user and model; Verevon chat-preview-truncation tests suggest partial coverage.

name: Session Log inspector with a DOM-to-log element picker (experimental)
what: An optional developer sidebar shows the raw session log or the Chat node tree as a virtualised table grouped by turn and step, with stream chunks as child rows, type filtering, a lazy object tree and a crosshair that maps a clicked Chat element back to its log record.
how: session-inspector registers a session-inspector-log sidebar page; rows grouped between turn/start and turn/end with nested step ranges; assistant stream blocks grouped under block-start; reference breadcrumbs between Node, Turn, Step and Data objects; the picker uses elementsFromPoint over a transparent mask and matches data attributes, never text similarity; enabled through the Developer Tools bundle in Plugin Manager.
verevonRelevance: A log inspector that bridges rendered chat and raw run records would speed support triage of Model Plane runs; keep it behind an org-admin permission because raw prompts and tool output are visible.
notes: Experimental and off by default (shipped switched off in Plugin Manager). Both inspectors are single-operator developer tools.

name: Chrome DevTools hub with full Host fetch capture (experimental)
what: An optional bottom panel embeds the Chrome DevTools frontend connected to the running Host and browser Clients: Console in each realm, Sources, the live Cordis plugin tree in Elements, and captured Host fetches (including model-provider requests) with full headers and bodies.
how: A Worker owns all CDP state; Host and Client collectors send versioned observation records (generation, sequence, source clock, topic) and CordisTreeSnapshots; Worker translates to Runtime, Network, Debugger and DOM domains; fetch capture wraps global fetch and stores bounded clones; Worker binds only to 127.0.0.1; Client ingest needs a random WebSocket subprotocol token.
verevonRelevance: Not suited to a multi-tenant product, but a local-development mode that records outbound provider HTTP is a cheap way to debug Model Plane adapters.
notes: Capture is unredacted and includes credentials; the CDP socket relies on loopback binding as its only access control (README Security section).

name: Configuration provenance dump (which layer set each row)
what: dsh --dump-config prints the composed plugin tree the process would boot as YAML, grouped under comments naming each row source and which later layers patched it; --dump-default-config omits user layers as a recovery diagnostic and --dump-config-schema prints a JSON Schema for entries and patches.
how: renderConfigDump applies layers cumulatively (bundles, profile cordis.patch.yml, home patch, --patch overlays), snapshots after each layer, compares JSON per row to attribute origin and patchedBy, emits "# == origin, patched by ..." separators, and warns with the layer label when a patch matches no row; no plugin is mounted and !!js is not evaluated.
verevonRelevance: Verevon layers plane env, org policy, Space and agent overrides; a per-value origin dump (who last set this) is the support tool for why an agent behaved differently.

name: Live plugin inventory and read-only preset composition viewer
what: Settings lists every loaded plugin with entry id, module, effective enablement (including disabled ancestors), live phase (pending, loading, active, failed, unloading), localized title, disabled conditions and discovery failures; agent-preset cards offer View configuration, opening the exact plugin list as read-only YAML.
how: pluginInventory/list Remote reads ctx.loader.entries() on every call (no cached second truth) and joins agent-preset compositionInventory; agentPresets/list and agentPresets/read supply the roster and YAML including !!js conditions; a broken preset stays readable because its diagnostic points into the YAML.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Agents page (AgentsPage, ChiefCoreRoutingPage) could show the exact tool and capability composition each agent role grants as a read-only document.

name: Startup failure report saved privately with credential warning
what: A failed boot prints a concise summary and saves the full original diagnostics to a uniquely named private file under DSH_HOME/logs with a warning that it may contain configuration or credential values; if writing fails the full report goes to stderr.
how: reportStartupFailure builds a util.inspect dump (depth null, showHidden) with version, node, platform, profile and the StartupError; writes with flag wx and mode 0600 in a 0700 directory; launcher context collects no environment values or plugin configs; a shipped rescue path is dsh <name> --from-default-profile web.
verevonRelevance: Pattern for a support bundle: short user-facing summary, full private report, explicit sharing warning; relevant to gateway diagnostics.

name: Generated, freshness-gated reference catalogs
what: Config, tool, persistence, CLI help and module-graph references are generated from source (config catalog has 152 plugin sections) and CI fails if the committed copy differs from a fresh regeneration.
how: scripts/gen-config-catalog.ts pastes each plugin Config declaration with JSDoc and cross-checks the runtime schemastery schema against the declaration; gen-tool-catalog boots tools to read live schemas; gen-persistence-catalog; gen-cli-help; verify-* scripts run in doc-sync; hand edits to generated regions are rejected.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already adopted a generated tool catalog (claude-hermes-deepseek.md 5.1); extending to a generated config and persistence catalog per plane would remove stale-doc risk.
notes: Partly adopted by Verevon according to its own adoption plan; the config and persistence catalogs are the new part.

name: Model Experience README contract (what the model sees, token effect, KV cache effect)
what: Every package README must end with a Model Experience section stating what the model sees, the token effect and the KV-cache effect of the package, or an audited sentence explaining why none applies; CI rejects missing or malformed sections.
how: verify-package-readme-model-experience.ts enforces heading order, three H4 fields per context entry, audited classifications (NO_MODEL_EXPERIENCE_SECTION, SENTENCE_MODEL_EXPERIENCE with reasons), generated-catalog links and final-section order; the cookbook defines KV-cache wording (append-only, stable prefix, replacement, independent request).
verevonRelevance: Strong fit for Verevon: planes that change prompts or context packs (Data Plane retrieval, Model Plane assembly, memory) could each document model-visible effect, token cost and cache impact, gated in CI.

name: User-path performance budgets with machine-profile scaled report
what: Required performance gates measure user paths (open and page a 240-turn session, first Trajectory, streaming while typing, session-open, terminal IO) in fresh processes on synthetic data and publish an HTML report that rescales each endpoint to modelled machines from a 2015 laptop to an M5 and AWS instances.
how: benchmarks/ organised by user path; workers built to lib/ and run under plain Node; recordTimings(case, timings, budgets) before asserting; scaled ms = ms x ((1-io) x cpuScore ratio x coreFactor + io x ioLatency ratio) using PassMark scores and storage latencies; reviewed constants (900/700/520 ms with 1.25x headroom); memory reruns under 4 GB and 8 GB cgroups; env vars cannot override budgets.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Frontend Plane could adopt user-path budgets for long chat threads and the agent console, with a shareable report instead of ad hoc timings.
notes: These gate product performance, not model quality. BENCHMARK.md only explains how to run the jsonrpc-agent minimal variant for external agent benchmarks; no results are published in the repo.

name: Recorded-session snapshot tests (log as input and expected output)
what: 600 committed session JSONL files across 227 scenario directories replay through shipped profiles without an API key and serve as the expected persisted output, with ARIA snapshots for the Web UI and committed expected workspace trees.
how: snapshots/{session,sdk,acp,web}; snapshot.yml declares profile and header class; typed tokens replace volatile ids and prompts and schemas move to sidecars; llm-replay supplies model output from the recorded log; every model- or user-visible change must update a scenario in the same PR; record and refresh scripts require review of every diff.
verevonRelevance: Recording real Model Plane run event streams and replaying them through the Frontend keylessly would harden chat rendering (Verevon has resume-replay controller tests but not committed recorded traces as fixtures).
notes: Counts via find on this checkout: scenario directories session 134, web 59, sdk 25, acp 9 (227 total); 600 .jsonl files.

name: Verify the world, not the agent self-report (testing policy)
what: End-to-end tests re-run commands or re-read files externally instead of trusting the agent output, assert untouched files are byte-identical, and compare the complete expected workspace tree for mutating scenarios.
how: docs/testing.md rule plus snapshot workspace.final with workspace.expected oracle that record and refresh never rewrite; real-API smoke tests per shipped profile; Model-only mocks (MockAdapter) with real tools and pipeline behind them.
verevonRelevance: Directly applicable to Verevon eval-lab-py and agent acceptance tests: assert external effects (documents, provider calls), not what the agent says.

name: Postmortems and decision notes as a public engineering ledger
what: Four numbered blameless postmortems (each opening with an executive summary and ending in guardrails) and thousands of decision notes with a closed class taxonomy, lifecycle folders (proposed, implemented, rejected, archived) and sealed, hash-checked archives.
how: docs/postmortem/*.md with required Executive summary; .agents/notes/{lifecycle}/{class}/yyyy-mm-dd-topic.md validated by verify-agent-note-format and verify-archived-agent-notes; archived triplets frozen with sidecar hashes; implemented notes kept current with shipped reality.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already created a postmortem and rejected-design ledger (adoption plan 7.6); the freeze-and-hash archive and lifecycle folders are additions.
notes: Inventory counted about 2,454 notes; not re-counted here.

name: Per-turn changed-files audit from private git snapshots
what: Each top-level turn ends with a changed-files card listing files changed with line counts and a review tab comparing turn start and end per file (unified or side by side), covering shell edits inside a git repository and file-tool edits elsewhere.
how: workspace-changes takes a git tree snapshot at turn start and end through a private index and temporary object directory (repository index, objects, refs untouched), diffs with diff-tree --numstat, copies each file-tool target whole before first edit by SHA-1, announces a workspace/changes event with only the turn number, and serves summary and per-file hunks (3 context lines, 100 ms diff timeout) from Host memory.
verevonRelevance: Agents that edit documents, Spaces or provider resources would benefit from a turn-scoped before/after audit that does not touch the user repository.
notes: Summaries live in Host memory; after a Host restart earlier turns have no card or comparison. Shell edits outside the snapshot coverage are not recorded. There is no undo or rewind of file state.

name: Session export as ZIP of the session tree
what: The session header menu and /export download the session, its sub-sessions and attachments as a ZIP of the raw logs.
how: session-log-export streams a ZIP from persistence read handles over an authenticated fetch route; compression level configurable (default 6); also offers a Feedback item when message feedback is mounted.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has chat export tests (ChatMessages.export.test.tsx); exporting the raw event log with attachments is the extra and supports data portability.

name: Raw event streams for SDK and headless consumers
what: External programs receive the full session events live (JSON-RPC session.event notifications, headless --json newline-delimited events) and Python runs return the event list, final response and finish reason.
how: HarnessSdkNotificationMap has session.event, session.status, subagent.started and subagent.finished; Python SDK run result carries events, final_response, finish_reason; dsh headless --json writes run events to stdout; both SDKs project the agent loop and are pinned by snapshots.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane generated SDKs could expose the same raw run events so customers can build their own audit and observability.

name: Wire disclosure reference for provider requests
what: One document lists every DeepSeek-Harness-specific HTTP header and additive JSON field sent on official requests (user-agent, anonymous user id, session id, compaction marker, dsh_plugin_packages, dsh_session_log), with schemas, defaults and the guarantee that they stay outside model input.
how: docs/deepseek-llm-api-wire-extensions.md defines namespaces (dsh_ prefix), per-field versions, the prepare/accept transaction after HTTP 2xx, omit-on-failure rules and collision failures; a DeepSeekLlmApiExtensionRegistry reserves one provider per field.
verevonRelevance: Verevon PROVIDER_AND_PRIVACY_STRATEGY.md could publish a generated list of every header and field each provider route receives, which also serves ZDR audits.
notes: The disclosed defaults are privacy-heavy for the official route (see the default-on session log upload record).

name: Human feedback stored as log-only events
what: Like and dislike with a category and note, and /feedback, are recorded as session events that never enter model context; the Web dialog is shared by the session and per-message entries.
how: feedback/record, feedback/message-put and feedback/message-delete events; ui-message-feedback decorates the message action row and opens one dialog; the feedback record is the authorization point for OTel session-log export (FEEDBACK_ONLY).
verevonRelevance: Verevon has a quality feature area; keeping ratings out of model context and tying any export to an explicit user act is a clean rule.

name: Subagent catalog with activity, usage and read-only history
what: The parent header lists local subagent conversations with activity, token usage and duration; continuable children accept follow-up prompts and Stop, historical one-shot children open read-only, and external tasks appear as non-navigable leaves.
how: ui-subagent catalog fed by subagent/catalog and subagent/descriptor events; the main sidebar omits subagent sessions; a separate @ reference source inserts a running child label without granting continuation authority; e2e tests cover activity and interrupt UI.
verevonRelevance: Verevon fleet and agent run consoles (FleetRunConsole, AgentRunConsole) can show per-child tokens and duration the same way.

name: Workflow run node shows identity and status only (transparency gap)
what: Durable workflow runs render as chat nodes with phases and members, but scripts, outputs, errors, logs, usage, topology and controls are deliberately outside the surface.
how: ui-workflow-run reconstructs tool-workflow/run-start, run-end, agent-start and agent-end events into nested disclosure; running, failed, cancelled and interrupted levels open by default; a running member can open its child session when local.
verevonRelevance: Cautionary example: when Verevon shows multi-step agent runs, include per-step output, error and usage, not only status.
notes: Limitation recorded from the package README; the Trajectory view can still show the underlying calls.

name: Account balance display and quota notice, but no per-turn currency cost
what: Desktop Settings shows the DeepSeek account balance and bonus wallets in CNY or USD and an embedded Usage page; quota failures raise a Top up modal. Chat shows token counts only, with no per-turn or per-session currency cost.
how: AccountSection reads balance wallets through the account Remote and formats with Platform Web rules (two decimals, sub-cent shown as <0.01, big.js for precision); AccountQuotaNotice claims ACCOUNT_QUOTA in the shell.quota-notice chain; a repository search of ui-chat and the token meter found no price tables.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already shows costUsd per turn and has CostDashboardPage; DSH shows the opposite choice (provider-side balance, token-only meters), which avoids stale price tables but hides cost.
notes: Corrects the scout inventory, which stated no balance display; a balance exists (Desktop only) but no per-turn cost.

name: Named permission presets bundling sandbox mode and approval policy
what: One Permissions picker (Read Only, Workspace Write, Full access, plus experimental Auto review) sets the file-sandbox mode and approval policy together; the choice is pinned per session, a default applies to future sessions, and unmatched combinations show as a derived custom state.
how: dsh-permission-presets owns a preset table in the base bundle (read-only and workspace-write use ask, danger-full-access uses never), a /permission command (bare call lists presets), a permission settings namespace for the default, and logs permission/preset, sandbox/mode and approval/policy events; resumed sessions keep their effective permission instead of the latest default.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has plan gates and ZDR refusals but no per-session capability preset the user can read; named presets with a logged selection would fit agent roles and Space policy.
notes: Corrects the scout inventory, which listed two presets; the base bundle ships three (read-only added).

name: Risk acknowledgement before Full access or Auto review
what: Choosing Full access or Auto review in the composer or /permission picker requires an explicit risk acknowledgement dialog, while the complete command /permission <preset> executes directly; the host confirms each change through the session projection.
how: ui-permission-presets renders General settings default row and the current-session picker; Auto shows an EXP badge and is excluded from settings defaults; the selection is confirmed by the Session projection rather than optimistic client state.
verevonRelevance: Verevon should require explicit acknowledgement before widening an agent power (browser actions, provider writes) and confirm from server state.

name: Fail-closed one-shot approval seam with deterministic never policy
what: Sensitive tool actions ask a human or machine answerer; no answerer, a throwing answerer or a stray return value resolves to unavailable and the action does not run; the never policy rejects without prompting (strict headless stance), and an approval applies to that one request only.
how: ApprovalService.request() appends approval/asked then approval/decided, races the answerer waterfall against the abort signal, normalises failures to unavailable and enforces never before waterfall dispatch so a later prepended listener cannot bypass it; the Web answerer takes over the composer with Enter to approve and Escape to reject.
verevonRelevance: Verevon prior analysis adopted similar guards; the never policy being enforced inside the service (not by listener order) is the detail to check in Model Plane approvals.

name: Approval audit pair without actor identity or persistent rules (gap)
what: Each approval writes a request event (tool, call id, reason) and one outcome event (allowed-once, rejected, cancelled, unavailable); the UI offers allow-once and reject only, so there are no always-allow rules and the log does not record who or what decided.
how: approval/asked {id, toolName, callId?, reason?} and approval/decided {id, outcome}; Web panel supports transient decisions only; persistent policy stays with Host-side packages; Auto review verdicts are not described as approval events; the README mentions reviewer reasons only on denial rows.
verevonRelevance: Verevon audit (Control Plane audit, RunProofPanel receipts) should record the deciding actor, channel and scope for every approval; copy the paired ask/decide shape but add identity.
notes: Inference from the type definitions: the outcome union has no decider field. Not checked against the Auto review listener beyond the README.

name: Permission policy is shown to the model and changes are announced
what: The model sees the current approval policy and sandbox meaning in its runtime context, and switching policy queues a sourced "changed by the user" message for the next step, while the human permission UI and audit events never enter model context.
how: system-prompt contribution approval:policy states the complete meaning of ask or never (fail-closed consequence or non-escalation) after retained history; setPolicy injects a sourced user message; a web e2e test pins permission-policy-context behaviour.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should tell the model its current permissions and announce changes mid-run so it does not plan around powers it lost.

name: Sandbox enforcement reported as a fact (full or partial), fail closed
what: Every confinement backend returns whether it fully or only partially enforces the requested mode, results show the selected mode, denied operations and enforcement level, and an unconfined fallback for a confined mode is never allowed (SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE instead).
how: ConfinedArgv {argv, enforcement, denialSignatures, runnerFailureRules}; policy resolved per capability call (SandboxExecutionPolicy with immutable cwd workspace root); Linux bwrap/Landlock, macOS Seatbelt, Windows ACL restricted-token backends; Windows and old Landlock ABIs are partial by their own README.
verevonRelevance: Already adopted in Verevon (claude-hermes-deepseek.md 5.1 item 3); the added part is surfacing enforcement level in the user-visible result rather than only in the backend.
notes: bash sandbox is disabled on win32 in the base bundle (pwsh sandbox used instead); network and process visibility are outside every mode.

name: Denial versus runner-failure attribution with visible markers
what: A command blocked by the sandbox is reported as a denial with a marker the model sees, while a failure of the sandbox runner itself is reported as infrastructure failure, never as an ordinary task failure.
how: Backend denialSignatures (EROFS under bwrap, EACCES under Landlock, EPERM under Seatbelt) are matched only after RunnerFailureRule checks (nonzero exit, allowed codes, fatal stderr line after informational exclusions); result carries sandbox {mode, denied}; denial marker text appended after bounded output; postmortem 0004 records the misclassification bug this prevents.
verevonRelevance: Useful pattern for Model Plane sandboxes (E2B-like runners) so users see why a command failed.
notes: Limitation stated in the README: denials are inferred from stderr, so a matching application error can be misread and a denial omitted from the retained tail can be missed.

name: Per-call escalation with narrowest wider mode and justification
what: When a command is denied, the model may retry the exact command once with sandbox_permissions set to the narrowest wider mode and a one-sentence justification, which the user sees and must approve before the wider mode runs.
how: bash, pwsh and run_code schemas expose sandbox_permissions plus justification; approved retries resolve a new per-call SandboxPolicy (no provider state mutated); recorded scenarios cover approved and rejected escalation for ACP and fs tools; a web e2e covers PTC escalation.
verevonRelevance: Codex and Claude Code have similar escalation; the one-sentence justification shown in the approval card is the part to copy for Verevon browser or provider actions.

name: Auto review: model-based per-call risk gate with isolated reviewer context (experimental)
what: An opt-in mode lets the current agent model review each native or inner PTC tool call before it runs under Full access: low-risk actions are allowed, medium-risk need explicit human or parent authorization, high-risk exfiltration is always denied, denials fall back to asking the user, and malformed or failed reviews never execute.
how: Prepended tools/pre-execute listener builds five sections from the session (fixed policy, cwd-only environment, sourced project constraints, filtered sourced history, complete pending action) and excludes main-agent system messages, assistant text and reasoning, and tool results; selecting Auto sets ask; delegated children pin never so denials are final; shipped off, installed through Plugin Manager with an EXP badge.
verevonRelevance: A reviewer that sees only user-sourced context and the action (not model prose or tool output) is a good prompt-injection posture for Model Plane browser and provider actions.
notes: README warns it can allow unsafe actions, deny useful work and spend extra tokens; kept off by default.

name: Credential references with UI-safe source disclosure and write-only keys
what: Settings and config carry credential references only; keys are write-only in the UI, the page shows whether a reference resolves, from which layer (environment, managed file, project or user .env) and whether it can be edited, and an environment-supplied key renders read-only because it would shadow any write.
how: CredentialRef brand; resolve() per operation (LLM adapters resolve per model request, so rotation needs no restart); describe() returns CredentialInfo {configured, source, writable} with no slot for the value; empty stored value is absent everywhere; settings forms redact secret-role fields and send presence markers.
verevonRelevance: Verevon connector and provider credentials could show source layer and writability (org policy vs user vs env) without exposing values; matches the gateway rule of never leaking upstream secrets.

name: Web trust fence: launch token, session cookie, Host/Origin check, trusted hosts
what: The GUI listens on loopback by default; a printed URL carries a process credential exchanged for a signed session cookie, requests are admitted only for loopback, the bind address and --trusted-host authorities (others get 403), wildcard binds are rejected at startup, and TLS can terminate on the listener or a proxy.
how: docs describe the fence as admission plus launch-token authentication; --public-url is display only; --tls-cert/--tls-key startup fails without falling back to HTTP; cookies Secure under TLS; Electron uses an authenticated IPC bridge instead of the server.
verevonRelevance: Verevon must not copy this: it is single-operator reachability control with no tenants or roles (prior analysis flagged it); copy only the docs candor about what the fence does not protect.
notes: Not exercised here beyond reading docs. The printed URL carries a credential, which the guide warns about.

name: Proxy and child-process environment hygiene
what: A project-level .env cannot set proxy variables because a cloned repository must not decide where traffic goes (the launcher refuses to start), diagnostics name a rejected variable without printing its URL, and MCP stdio children get credential-like and DSH_* variables stripped.
how: Proxy variables are read from the shell or DSH_HOME/.env only; the stdio bridge removes ambient variables whose names usually identify credentials and all DSH_* before launching a child, with explicit config.env for needed secrets.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to Verevon sandboxes and MCP-like connectors: never let repository or tenant content choose network routes, and scrub inherited secrets for child processes.

name: Feedback-gated session telemetry with disclosure, redaction waterfall and opt-out
what: Session logs leave the machine through OpenTelemetry only after the user submits explicit feedback (FEEDBACK_ONLY) and never on ordinary activity; DISABLED constructs no transport; an environment variable opts the process out; every outbound record passes a fail-closed redaction waterfall.
how: session-telemetry-otel authorises the unhanded prefix on feedback events, one record per event with redacted data; Resource carries an anonymous UUID in DSH_HOME/.anonymous-user-id (delete to reset); DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED (any non-empty value) disables; sessionTelemetry/record waterfall withholds a record if a listener throws and redaction never rewrites the canonical log; sharing property reports feedback-only or disabled.
verevonRelevance: Pattern for Verevon quality and support exports: authorisation tied to an explicit user act, a disclosure property, fail-closed redaction, and canonical data never rewritten.
notes: The default collector is a DeepSeek-operated URL (https://dsh-otel-collector.deepseeksvc.com/v1/logs) overridable by DSH_TELEMETRY_OTLP_URL.

name: Default-on provider-side session-log upload and plugin inventory (opt-out)
what: On the official DeepSeek route every request carries the next suffix of the canonical session log (up to 8 MiB) and the list of active plugin packages as request-body fields outside model input; Settings has a switch for the session log, the plugin inventory has only a config toggle.
how: dsh_session_log (acceptance watermark in session-log-deepseek/delivery-accepted, at-least-once) and dsh_plugin_packages (name and version) registered through DeepSeekLlmApiExtensionRegistry; enabled defaults true; Settings General switch writes the plugin enabled field; no UI control for the inventory field was found.
verevonRelevance: Anti-pattern for Verevon ZDR and tenant rules: default-on upload of conversation logs to a provider; but the documented fields, visible switch and watermark acceptance design are worth studying.
notes: Transparent by documentation, opt-out by default. Applies to the official DeepSeek route only; pi-ai routes do not implement these fields (wire-extensions doc).

name: Cross-session recall authorised by exact working directory and marked untrusted
what: Model tools that search or read earlier sessions only authorise targets whose cwd exactly matches the caller, callers without a cwd can inspect only themselves, and @session references are inserted as bounded read-only snapshots under a fixed warning that they are untrusted background and must not be obeyed.
how: tool-session-query (five read-only tools, opt-in) authorises by cwd equality and excludes the caller from search; session-reference prepares immutable snapshots carrying a warning against following instructions or permission claims; base bundle keeps content search off (session-query-sqlite openAt never) so sidebar search matches titles and workspace names only.
verevonRelevance: Maps to Verevon rule that Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL: authorise recall by explicit scope equality and label recalled content as untrusted data.
notes: Corrects the scout inventory: content search is shipped disabled; the tools sit under packages/experimental.

name: Plugin installation gated like Full access and runs outside the sandbox
what: The plugin_manager tool (enabled in Creator mode only) needs danger-full-access or per-call approval, and the docs state installed Host code executes in-process outside the workspace sandbox; dependency build scripts need a separate approval.
how: Plugin Manager tool actions require approval under lower sandbox modes (never or rejection prevents execution); install failure restores package.json and lockfile; inspect(spec) reads registry metadata before installing; official on-demand bundles install pinned to the running DSH version.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon marketplace or connector installs: show what will be read before install, restore on failure, and state the trust level of installed code.

name: Skill invocation policy separates model-invocable and user-invocable skills
what: Each skill carries modelInvocable and userInvocable flags so the registry can serve the model catalog and human slash commands differently without conflating them.
how: ctx.skills registry fills a default invocation policy and provider label; the registry keeps all four flag combinations; skill-invocation-policy e2e and skill-user-invoke tests cover surfaces.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agent blueprints and skills could mark which are user-triggerable versus agent-triggerable, a governance control for tenants.

name: Subagent model-route allowlist recorded per session and inherited
what: Users choose which exact provider/model routes agents may select when delegating to subagents; the sampled list is recorded in the session, inherited by child sessions and unaffected by later settings edits, and a Settings page also sets delegation depth and width.
how: modelSelectionSettings samples the subagent-model-selection preference when a fresh top-level session is composed and records subagent/model-selection-policy; list_subagent_models plus route validation before delegation; ui-settings-subagent stages both namespaces under one save.
verevonRelevance: A user- or org-controlled allowlist of models an agent may spend on is a direct cost and data-residency control for Model Plane routing and Control Plane entitlements.

name: Safety notice states plainly that sandboxes and approvals do not guarantee isolation
what: SAFETY.md says the project is experimental, unaudited and not production-ready, that sandboxes and approvals reduce risk but do not guarantee isolation, and gives responsible-use steps (least privilege, disposable VM, backups, review plugins).
how: Static document linked from the README run instructions; the sandbox docs repeat that network and process visibility are outside the guarantees.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agent pages could state the real limits of its guardrails next to the controls (what ZDR, sandboxing and approvals do not cover).

name: Privacy disclosure when displayed reasoning is sent to an external translator (experimental)
what: The optional reasoning-translation bundle states that translating expanded reasoning sends the displayed text to the chosen external service, which may include private code, keeps the original in the session, and lets the user switch back to the original at any time.
how: Plugin bundle with provider (Bing default, Google, DeepSeek Flash) and target language set in Plugins; wrapper registered in the conversation.chat.reasoning.body slot; results stored durably and reused; failure keeps the original with Retry.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon feature that forwards content to a third party (translation, voice) should carry an in-product disclosure at the point of enablement, consistent with PROVIDER_AND_PRIVACY_STRATEGY.

name: Desktop quit and update warnings name what would be interrupted
what: Quitting or installing an update asks the Host what it would interrupt (running agents including subagents and approval waits, queued messages, running jobs, armed scheduled reminders) and shows a specific explanation, while failure details sit behind a collapsed View technical details.
how: Private IPC channel returns two facts for the quit check; native message box with Quit default and Cancel on Esc; update restart drains admitted requests and rechecks tasks; typed preparation causes select localized guidance; technical details show only exit status, signal, acknowledgement and deadline facts, not plugin stderr.
verevonRelevance: Web analogue: warn before archiving, signing out, changing org policy or deploying with running agent runs or queued work, naming exactly what will stop.

name: Work-details modes: four levels of process visibility plus collapse timing
what: Settings offer Compact, Standard, Detailed and Verbose work details that decide how much tool and reasoning process shows around the final answer, and a separate collapse-timing preference (on completion or on next message); defaults differ by client (Desktop Standard, Web Detailed).
how: ui-chat.transcriptView host setting (legacy normal and expanded values read as detailed and are never written back); visibility applies outside in: whole turn, then process group, then individual reasoning or tool body; collapse timing is client-instance only and never persisted; final answers are never hidden.
verevonRelevance: Verevon StepsPanel and run console show one fixed level of detail; user-selectable process visibility (including a verbose flat mode) would serve both casual and audit users.

name: Performance and usage detail level (compact or detailed)
what: A two-level preference controls the composer statistics: Compact shows only output speed and cache-hit percentage without dialogs or per-turn usage; Detailed adds session statistics dialogs and the per-turn usage row; the preference never changes accounting or events.
how: ui-chat.performanceUsage in ChatSettings schema (default detailed); PerformanceUsagePolicy store reconciles accepted Host settings and publishes immediately; process-local on non-loopback browsers whose settings cannot persist.
verevonRelevance: Verevon could expose a similar toggle so metrics are available to power users without cluttering the default chat.

name: Running and closed activity titles with fixed category vocabulary
what: Process groups carry a one-line title built from a fixed vocabulary (Reading files, Searching code, Running commands, Running code, Searching the web, Coordinating subagents, Updating the plan, Waiting for your action) with live detail in Standard mode; running titles stay visible at least 150 ms and closed titles name the top three categories.
how: Tool-name classification maps each tool to a category with preparing, running and closed labels; closed group header uses ranked summary without counts; counts never decide folding; process-groups.ts and step-process.ts implement segmentation; locale keys message.stepProcess.*.
verevonRelevance: A fixed category vocabulary for agent activity lines (Verevon workStepLabel in ChatPanels.tsx has a similar idea) keeps live status honest and localisable.

name: Reasoning disclosure with streaming preview and replaceable body
what: Reasoning is a collapsed Think row whose preview shows the first line (or the latest completed paragraph while streaming) with a shimmer; expanding shows full compact Markdown; plugins can wrap the body, for example to translate it.
how: ReasoningRow with DisclosureRow, latestCompletedParagraphFirstLine, preview gated by the work-details policy (hidden in Compact when settled); conversation.chat.reasoning.body single slot and conversation.chat.reasoning.content factory; mode switches toggle CSS display without unmounting.
verevonRelevance: Verevon ReasoningTrace and the Details popover Insight tab are comparable; the paragraph-boundary preview rule avoids flicker.

name: Staged settings pages with override markers, reset-to-default and stale-write refusal
what: Plugin settings pages stage typed values and write only on save, mark values the user overrode, offer to reset each to the deployment default, refuse edits that a higher layer (home patch or --patch overlay) would override, and keep drafts when another writer changed the value.
how: ctx.configForms snapshots carry resolved value, inherited base, raw user value, revision, writability and persistence mode; set, unset and mutate submit one atomic operation list with the revision read before editing; Settings validates the complete Config and refuses stale revisions before persistence; Reset restores the value beneath the profile override.
verevonRelevance: Verevon settings (router-policy, billing, org policy) need exactly this three-layer view (effective, inherited, own) with optimistic concurrency; copy the descriptor shape.

name: Open configuration file escape hatch from Settings
what: On a loopback browser Settings offers Open configuration file, which opens the profile cordis.patch.yml in the native editor; remote browsers never get the action or the privileged read, and adapters re-read the file on the next request so no restart is needed.
how: settings/describe reports hasDocument; settings/openSettingsDocument is a pathless browser-authenticated Remote that resolves the provider path again, creates an absent document and launches the platform editor (open -t on macOS, association on Linux and Windows, wslpath on WSL); HMR applies the change live.
verevonRelevance: Power-user customisation for Verevon (agent role definitions, router policy) could offer a diffable YAML or JSON view with the same effective/override semantics.
notes: Single-machine feature; meaningless for a hosted multi-tenant web app, where a downloadable and re-importable config would be the analogue.

name: Coding Tools switch as progressive disclosure of developer features
what: A General setting hides developer-oriented surfaces (PTC and Minimal presets, changed-files card, HTML preview permissions) while keeping Standard, Creator and custom presets, so casual users see a simpler product.
how: ctx.configForms.developerTools owns ui-settings.enabled (default true); Host-backed clients keep developer features disabled until the first accepted value; turning it off resets a saved PTC or Minimal default to Standard; it controls presentation and preview permissions, not Host authorization or session recording.
verevonRelevance: Verevon could use a single complexity switch (basic or advanced) to gate trace, tool and routing panels per user.
notes: Explicitly presentation-only; it is not a security control.

name: Theme, separate font controls and first-paint bootstrap
what: Users pick light, dark or system and set font and size for text, code and terminal separately; values persist in the ui-theme settings namespace and a synchronous bootstrap applies palette, size and fonts before the shell loads to avoid a flash.
how: ui-theme publishes immutable ThemeSnapshots applied by ui-layout; --dsw-* token stylesheets; third-party themes register alias-token overrides through ctx.theme; loopback clients persist to the profile patch, others stay process-local.
verevonRelevance: Separate code and text font settings and a no-flash bootstrap are low-cost wins for Verevon chat code blocks.

name: Shortcut reference with rebinding and fixed input actions
what: Mod+/ opens a searchable reference of commands available in the current window (by action, alias or key); bindings can be recorded, cleared or restored, while fixed input actions stay read-only; Desktop stores overrides in a separate keybindings.json and intercepts bindings natively.
how: packages/client/shortcuts registry with physical-key routing and recording; ui-shortcuts reference; Desktop keybindings.json validated by the main process, failed reads block edits including Restore All, two-key chords supported without native accelerators.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has chat shortcuts (use-chat-shortcuts.test.ts); a searchable reference and conflict-aware rebinding would improve discoverability.

name: Double-Escape stop bound to the live turn and focused region
what: Stopping a running turn needs two independent Escape presses within a short interval, validated against the freshly resolved live turn, session generation and focused input region so a stale press cannot cancel the wrong turn.
how: StopSequence holds one short-lived first press with a target {sessionId, turn, generation, region, cancel}; reset on expiry or mismatch; non-repeated Escape only; pending queued work resumes in FIFO order after cancel.
verevonRelevance: Guard against accidental stops of long agent runs in Verevon chat, bound to run id.

name: Queue dock and steering with editable pending work
what: While a turn runs, new prompts can be queued or used to steer the running turn; pending queue items can be edited, removed or promoted to steering, cancelling the current turn keeps the queue in FIFO order, and local echoes disappear atomically when the authoritative record arrives.
how: prompt(content, mode: queue|steer) and an action API that applies edit, remove or steer to a pending occurrence; QueueDock renders pending rows; Inbox projection orders steering across clients; browser e2e covers edit, remove and stop.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has mid-run-input tests (mid-run-input.test.ts); editable queued and steering rows with atomic echo replacement would round it out.

name: Typed slot system lets plugins add or replace any UI element by id
what: The Web client UI is composed from typed slots; a plugin can add or replace one piece (for example one composer statistics pill) by registering the same id and order, with priority choosing the replacement, and registrations unwind when the plugin unloads.
how: ctx.slots.register and inject with declaration-merged SlotMap (key, cardinality, scope, owner props); ui-renderer renders root through renderSlot; undeclared slots fail at activation; effects dispose child slots; dock entries carry data-composer-stat ids.
verevonRelevance: Verevon Frontend Plane has action contracts (src/shared/actions) and no slot registry was found in src/shared; slots would let enterprise tenants or plane teams customise panels without forks.
notes: High engineering cost; the TypeScript declaration-merging approach is JS-specific, but the id/order/priority replacement rule transfers to Solid.

name: Slash commands never downgrade to prompts; human commands stay out of model history
what: A typed slash line either opens a popup, runs a client action, takes input or executes directly; it is never silently sent as a plain prompt. Human commands run against the agent without creating a model message, are recorded in the session log, and render outside model history.
how: ctx.commands registry (lowercase name, description, input hint, handler returning success or error), command/run and command/done log events with source kind user, recordInput flag; ui-commands resolves popupSelect, action, leadingInput or execute against the session directory; commands can accept attachments with enforced declarations.
verevonRelevance: Separating human control commands (permission, compact, export) from model messages keeps the model context clean and the audit log honest in Verevon chat.

name: Onboarding as a one-step-at-a-time ledger with versioned notices
what: First-run onboarding steps register into an ordered ledger and exactly one mounts at a time; each owner stores its own durable completion, skip or complete hands over to the next, and the Models page walks first-run users through a versioned preview notice and a conditional official-credential step.
how: settings.onboarding slot projects ascending order; the shell mounts one step with complete() and openSection(id); registrants own copy, mutations and wrapper; Desktop has a welcome window and API-key onboarding IPC.
verevonRelevance: Verevon onboarding (onboarding feature) could adopt per-step ownership of completion state so new planes add steps without stacking dialogs.

name: Whole-log turn outline and virtual turn rail navigation
what: A side rail shows a mark for every turn of the session, including unloaded ones, with prompt and response previews; clicking pages history from the exact event sequence needed and lands on the turn.
how: session-turn-outline projection gives every started turn with bounded prompt and settled-response previews (excluding injected context and tool results); TurnNavigator is a fixed-pitch virtual rail (10 px) with preview, busy pulse and reduced-motion aware scrolling.
verevonRelevance: Long Verevon threads and agent runs benefit from a minimap that works before history is loaded; needs a server-side outline projection.

name: Browser find reveals text inside collapsed work details
what: Collapsed process rows stay in the DOM with hidden=until-found so Ctrl+F finds text inside them and expands the row on match, instead of unmounting content.
how: useSearchableHidden sets hidden until-found and listens for beforematch to call reveal; avoids hiding when focus is inside; hooked to disclosure state and transitions.
verevonRelevance: Easy win for Verevon collapsed reasoning and tool details: native find works inside folded content.
notes: Chromium feature; Safari and Firefox support differs.

name: Locale-owned UI copy enforced by a gate, with dictionary parity checks
what: All product text routes through typed locale dictionaries (English and Chinese); a gate rejects hardcoded copy and a parity test keeps both dictionaries aligned, so every transparency label above exists in both languages.
how: AGENTS.md rule plus verify-client-ui-i18n and locale-dictionary-parity specs; typed translate seats per package namespace; typed failure causes select localized guidance so wording changes cannot reclassify failures.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already supports Norwegian and English (i18n.tr pairs inline in components); a lint gate against hardcoded strings and a parity test would remove drift.
notes: Inline i18n.tr pairs in Verevon components bypass dictionary parity checks.

name: Feedback-surface rules: toast versus in-place notice, failed operations keep data
what: A UI skill codifies where messages appear: transient outcomes use an app-wide Toast held in a shell overlay so it survives the closing panel, states tied to a surface use an in-place notice, a failed operation keeps its data visible, copy is plain and short, and every menu must be dismissable, viewport-fitting and unclipped.
how: .agents/skills/dsh-client-ui-ux/SKILL.md plus dsh-error-handling skill; Settings and quota notices follow the pattern (shell.overlay entries, shell.quota-notice chain with keepOpen).
verevonRelevance: A short written UX contract for feedback surfaces would reduce inconsistent error handling across Verevon features.

name: Connection status with hold times and priority over update status
what: A pill shows Disconnected, Reconnecting (with advancing dots, at least 800 ms visible) and Connected (for two seconds) while healthy operation stays silent; clicking retries immediately; connection feedback outranks Desktop update status except during installation.
how: ConnectionIndicator in ui-settings-general with min-visible hold and recovered timer; consumes ctx.connection.state and reconnect(); Connection client uses generation, readiness and gap repair.

name: PWA install metadata and a tested startup RPC budget

name: Docked three-column layout with plugin-registered sidebar tabs

name: Ask-user question card with timed wait, drafts and late replies

name: Provider forms: catalog providers, custom endpoints and three wire protocols

how: llm-pi-ai routes pi-ai providers and OpenAI-compatible gateways from one configuration resolved per request (no restart); the Models page writes the active profile cordis.patch.yml; API protocol stored as openai-completions, openai-responses or anthropic-messages; a provider speaks one protocol; built-in provider catalog supplies endpoint, protocol and models.
verevonRelevance: Verevon routes via Model Plane router-policy; a bring-your-own-endpoint form with explicit protocol selection and a permanent id would support enterprise gateways.
