name: Model discovery that is explicit about what it cannot guarantee
what: Fetch available models asks an endpoint what it serves and opens a searchable picker, stores nothing until save, and the guide states discovery is a convenience (not every endpoint answers) and that built-in providers are always answered from the installed catalog.
how: Reads common GET /models listing formats (data array or models object) using the form key or the stored key; troubleshooting names the two failure messages and tells the user to add ids by hand.
verevonRelevance: Candid limits next to a convenience feature reduce support load for Verevon connector and model setup.

name: Per-model reasoning-effort vocabulary mapped to the wire value
what: The model picker shows an Effort menu when a model declares levels (DeepSeek: off, low, high, max); custom models declare their own level names and the wire spelling, an unsupported effort is refused before any network call, and a thinkingFormat switch handles gateways that need thinking enabled or disabled objects.
how: reasoningEfforts map {level: wire value} per model (off may be empty = parameter absent); route-level reasoning default; compat.thinkingFormat deepseek sends thinking {type: enabled|disabled} beside the effort; UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT error; DeepSeek adapter serialises low/high/max as output_config.effort and off as thinking disabled; llm-deepseek.reasoningEffort sets the picker default.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane routing should expose a per-model effort vocabulary and refuse unsupported values before dispatch; users then see only levels the route can honour.

name: Request-compat switches documented as claims, not checks
what: Gateway quirks (system prompt role developer versus system, max_tokens versus max_completion_tokens, thinking format, image input modalities) are set per route or per model; the guide says each switch states a claim about the endpoint that is not verified, empty values are refused, unknown names list the valid ones, and a troubleshooting table maps symptoms to switches.
how: compat {supportsDeveloperRole, maxTokensField, thinkingFormat} with model overriding route field by field over the catalog value; input and defaultInput modalities; empty compat key refused rather than ignored; PiAiCompatProfile documented in the generated config catalog.
verevonRelevance: For Verevon custom gateway or on-prem models, per-route compat overrides plus symptom-keyed troubleshooting would make integration self-serve.

name: Model selection semantics: next request, per session, blocked when unavailable
what: Switching model or effort through /model or the composer applies to the next request while a running step keeps the model it started with; a session that already sent a request keeps the model in its log; if a saved default names a deleted provider the composer is disabled and shows Select model.
how: ui-model-selection presents one provider-grouped directory for both surfaces; model/selection events and request/header record the chosen route; selecting also sets the default for new sessions; a model-menu observer test covers the picker (also in WebKit).
verevonRelevance: Verevon should make explicit that a model change applies from the next turn and is recorded per message; a blocked composer for a vanished model is better than a silent fallback.
notes: No cross-provider failover was found (scout negative finding); a missing model blocks instead.

name: Retry policy per provider route with normal and always modes
what: Each provider route sets how failed requests are retried: normal mode (five retries for EMPTY_RESPONSE, RATE_LIMIT, SERVER, TIMEOUT, TRANSPORT with 500 ms to 10 s backoff and jitter) or always mode (unlimited until success or cancel), with the docs warning that each retry is billed.
how: retryPolicy {mode, backoff{initialDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitterRatio}, eligible codes} on the adapter; dsh-llm-retry executes it at durable step boundaries; Retry-After honoured within bounds; always mode asks downstream recovery first.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane retry and fallback policy could be a per-route, user-visible setting with a stated billing consequence.

name: Per-model compaction policy with separate summarisation route
what: Compaction triggers at floor(min(W x 0.8, W - O - 65,536)), retains the newest 16 percent verbatim, and can be overridden per exact provider/model (threshold, retain tokens) with its own summarisation provider and model and a separate output cap; misconfiguration fails at load.
how: compaction-basic config {thresholdRatio, headroomTokens, retainRatio or retainTokens, summarizationProvider/Model, maxTokens, compactionRetries, maxOverflowRetries, modelPolicies[], auto}; overflow recovery after a confirmed context-window error; manual /compact; tool-result pruner (8,192 char threshold) runs first; image offload on image-budget rejections.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane context management should publish its trigger formula and allow a cheaper summarisation model per route; users could see and tune it per agent.

name: Cache-aware design choices exposed as documented behaviour
what: Several choices exist for provider prompt-cache reuse and are written down: the tool catalog stays identical across plan mode and normal mode, fork subagents omit model selection so provider and model equal the parent, in-history system updates append after cached history on capable routes, and cache hit is reported to the user.
how: Base bundle plan-mode section text states the catalog rule; tool-subagent fork config comment; RequestContext.systemPromptUpdate in-history capability; Model Experience KV Cache effect per package; llm-deepseek reports cache read and write usage; Trajectory shows cached and cache-created tokens.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane should treat prompt-cache stability as a design constraint (stable tool order, append-only system updates) and show cache read per turn so cost effects are explainable.

name: Image request budgets with logged offload decisions and priced placeholders
what: Images are normalised to the provider vision grid, uploaded through the Files API (inline base64 only as fallback), and when a request exceeds byte or count budgets the oldest images are replaced by named placeholders through a logged image/offload event; the token meter prices placeholders and images separately.
how: llm-deepseek image limits (imagePixelBudget, imageMaxBytes, maxRequestFilesBytes 128 MiB, maxImagesPerRequest 600, offload quanta) and IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED naming the occurrences to offload; compaction-image-offload records image/offload; imageRequestPricing supplies visual tokens per occurrence; each retained image is preceded by text with id and dimensions.
verevonRelevance: Verevon attachment handling for vision routes should log offload decisions and tell the model and user which images were dropped.

name: Account route versus API-key route kept strictly separate
what: The deepseek-official route resolves only its configured API key and the deepseek-account route only the stored sign-in grant; neither falls back to the other, signing out removes the grant but keeps API keys, tokens go in different headers, and neither follows redirects.
how: x-dsh-auth-token for account tokens (no Bearer) versus x-api-key; allowed inferenceOrigin for the account route; credential failures happen before the anonymous-id header is created; INVALID_CREDENTIAL names the reference to fix, never part of the key.
verevonRelevance: Control-plane issued tokens versus customer-supplied provider keys in Verevon should likewise never fall back to each other silently.

name: Editable model catalog per provider (context window, max output, input types) with Restore defaults
what: The Models page lets users edit each model id, display name, context window, max output tokens and input types (text, image); the guide explains inherited values are shown without saving an override and that Restore defaults removes the whole model-catalog override.
how: Model options row under Customized settings writes input for pi-ai models and inputModalities for the direct adapter; modelOverrides keyed by model id for built-in providers; at least one modality must stay selected; clearing Image also removes image limits DeepSeek rejects on text-only models.
verevonRelevance: Model capability overrides (context window, modalities) visible and editable per route would let Verevon admins correct catalog gaps without code changes.

name: Benchmark profile sdk-minimal: no telemetry, settings or extras
what: A standalone profile gives an SDK client a small explicit coding-agent runtime (persistent shell, working_directory, uncompressed JSONL sessions, model from the initialize request) that excludes base bundle features such as telemetry, settings, compaction, skills, jobs and subagents, intended for isolated benchmark workspaces.
how: dsh --profile sdk-minimal is a complete bundle (does not apply dsh-base); Python SDK launches it with an explicit DSH_HOME and never silently reads ~/.dsh; BENCHMARK.md says to use separate workspaces and session ids per independent task.
verevonRelevance: Verevon eval-lab runs would benefit from a minimal, telemetry-free agent profile with explicit home and workspace for reproducible measurements.
notes: Its danger-full-access policy means the benchmark workspace must be disposable.

name: Auxiliary model requests are logged before dispatch
what: Session-title generation and DeepSeek web-search requests are recorded in the session log as secret-free pre-dispatch events with the exact system text, messages, output-token cap and reasoning effort, so side calls are as auditable as the main conversation.
how: "session/title-llm-request" (SessionTitleLlmRequestEventData: system, messages, maxTokens, reasoningEffort) and "web/deepseek-search-llm-request" are log-only events appended before the request; both are in the known event vocabulary; title requests carry the live session id and compaction requests carry a purpose header.
verevonRelevance: Verevon background model calls (titles, follow-ups, router decisions, memory) should be visible and countable in the same ledger as the main run so cost and privacy audits are complete.

name: Profiles and layered bundles as the customisation surface
what: The running app is a plugin tree composed from ordered layers (shipped bundles, the profile cordis.patch.yml, a home patch, --patch overlays); a patch replaces a row by id or inserts rows, users can create a profile from a shipped template, and every row printed by --dump-config can be replaced by a patch.
how: dsh --profile <name> with templates web, headless, sdk, sdk-minimal and acp; dsh-base is the shared first layer; patch replaces the whole row config (documented rule); !!js allowed only under plugin config and disabled; HMR is controlled by YAML; rescue profile via --from-default-profile.
verevonRelevance: Verevon could express per-tenant and per-agent customisation as ordered patch layers over a base composition with a provenance dump, instead of scattered feature flags.
notes: Everything is a plugin: even the model adapter, session log and agent loop are replaceable from config (Cordis).

name: Plugins page: bundles and rows on or off, official experimental group, cancellable installs
what: The sidebar Plugins page switches bundles and individual plugin rows on and off, lists official optional (Experimental) bundles shipped switched off, installs third-party bundles from a package name, Git repository or local directory after showing what the spec names, streams pnpm output, supports cancel, and lets the agent create a plugin in Creator mode.
how: plugin-manager service (listBundles, inspect, installBundle with requestId, cancelInstall, registry fallback plan, failure restores package.json and lockfile); a toggle edits only disabled in the last matching override or appends one; bundle toggle edits dsh.profile.bundles order; plugin-manager/changed events; e2e tests cover registry, GitHub, approve and cancel flows.
verevonRelevance: Verevon integrations and agent marketplace pages could adopt install preview, progress streaming, cancel and rollback on failure.
notes: Installed host code runs in-process outside the sandbox (see the governance record).

name: Agent presets as user-visible modes pinned per session
what: A preset (Standard, PTC, Minimal, Creator and custom) defines a session child plugin list and therefore its tools and prompt; the preset id is stored in the session header so resume replays against the same composition, the picker explains each mode, and a custom group is user-owned.
how: agent-preset rows with id, plugins, name, description, order; agent-preset-registry default; session header agentPreset field ("durable because the preset decides tools and prompt"); agentPresets/list and read Remotes; persona row shadows the deployment persona per preset; creator mode mounts bundled authoring skills.
verevonRelevance: Verevon agent roles (agent-roles.ts, verevon-agent-blueprints.tsx) could be pinned per run and expose a read-only composition view for auditors.

name: System prompt composed from ordered named sections with a configurable tool order
what: The system prompt is assembled from named sections with explicit order values (fixed harness opener, persona prefix at 0, first-party guidance, persona suffix at 10200) and variables; config sets persona text, whether to include runtime context, and an explicit model-facing tool order; invalid complete-prompt combinations fail assembly instead of sending a malformed prompt.
how: ctx.systemPrompt.section({name, order, text, complete, interpolate}); getSectionOrder and getContextOrder central allocation for repository contributors; agent-scoped contributions shadow same-named globals; toolOrder with one rest entry; includeHarnessIdentity; refreshContext re-reads registered runtime facts before admission.
verevonRelevance: Model Plane prompt assembly could use named, ordered sections whose list is inspectable per request (paired with the request header record).

name: Hook bridges that reuse existing Claude Code and Codex hooks (experimental)
what: Users point a bridge at an existing hooks.json so command hooks can block a prompt or tool call with a message the model sees, add context, or ask the run to stop; hook handlers other than command are skipped with a warning, and hook invocations and results are logged.
how: dsh-hook-protocol defines hook semantics shared by hooks-claude-code and hooks-codex; hook/invoked and hook/result session events; tools/pre-execute waterfall integration.
verevonRelevance: Lets customers bring existing policy hooks; for Verevon, org-level pre-tool policy hooks with logged results would fit the audit story.
notes: Experimental; not exercised here.

name: Model-facing introspection of the live plugin composition (cordis_inspect tools)
what: Agents in Creator mode can list and query the Host Inspect Providers and read package READMEs and config surfaces before authoring a plugin, so the model works from the real composition instead of guessing.
how: dsh-tool-cordis registers cordis_inspect_list and cordis_inspect_query; creator-mode skills tell the agent to read inspection results first, then the package README under packageDir reported by Config.listConfigs; process-local runtime plugin definitions do not survive restart.
verevonRelevance: A read-only self-description tool (which tools, policies and limits apply to this run) would reduce hallucinated capability claims in Verevon agents.

name: Default-off reference overlays for third-party MCP memory servers with pinned versions
what: Three memory MCP systems ship only as copy-paste overlays enabled with --patch or by merging one insert into a user patch; the guide pins tested versions and commit SHAs, says DSH does not install or supervise them, and states it implies no endorsement.
how: dsh-mcp-client launches stdio or connects Streamable HTTP, discovers tools as mcp__server__tool; stdio children get credential-like ambient variables and DSH_* removed; overlays live under apps/cli/config/examples/mcp-memory.
verevonRelevance: Pinned, default-off connector recipes with explicit responsibility boundaries suit Verevon integration docs.
notes: Memory is external (MCP); DSH has no built-in learned memory.

name: Workspace instruction files with a visible budget notice
what: User-global and project AGENTS.md-compatible files are injected into context under a byte budget (default 65,536); broader files are dropped before the most specific file is truncated, and a visible notice names omitted and truncated paths; added, updated or removed instruction files appear as context rows in the transcript.
how: dsh-agent-instructions loads the chain for the first request, discovers nested files after filesystem operations, reconciles on resume; config maxBytes, maxSourceBytes, projectRootMarkers, instructionFileCandidates and local overlays; ContextForm instructions rows show loaded, added, updated, removed.
verevonRelevance: Verevon org and Space instructions injected into runs should have a byte budget and a visible notice when anything was dropped or truncated.
notes: No learned memory or self-created skills exist in DSH; personalization is file-based.

name: Advisory repeat-call reminders at visible thresholds
what: When the model calls the same tool with identical arguments repeatedly, reminders at 3, 5 and 8 repeats ask it to inspect the previous result and change approach or finish; the reminder never blocks a legitimate repeat and resets on a new user message.
how: dsh-repeat-tool-reminder on the tools chain with thresholds [3, 5, 8] and argumentsPreviewChars 500, tracked per agent; timeout-policy separately returns a clear timeout error after cooperative cancellation settles.
verevonRelevance: A soft loop-breaker with configurable thresholds is a low-risk guard for Model Plane tool loops; Verevon could surface it as a visible nudge row.
notes: Advisory only; it does not stop runaway loops.

name: Durable goals with compare-and-set edits and a visible goal bar
what: One long-running objective persists across turns, resume, fork and restart; users and agents can create, edit, pause, resume, complete, block or clear it, stale edits are rejected, a round cap (256 default) bounds automatic continuation, blocked goals keep a stable policy code with an explanation, and a bar above the composer shows durable state and current activation.
how: dsh-goal with goal/change events and compare-and-set updates; goal-round-driver continues through agent events; continuation permission is process-local, not durable; ui-goal edits, pauses, resumes, clears and shows /goal runs as command bubbles; goal rounds are labelled in message source.
verevonRelevance: Verevon long-running agent objectives could show durable goal state, round count against a cap and the blocked reason.

name: Plan mode with a reviewed plan, honest that it is advisory
what: /plan makes the agent explore and design first and then present a plan for approval in the right sidebar; the user approves, rejects with feedback or dismisses, the plan reloads from session history, and the docs state every tool stays available so sandbox and approval prompts are the enforced limits.
how: dsh-plan-mode with plan/mode events and an exit_plan_mode tool taking complete plan markdown; guidance text is configurable YAML in the base bundle and keeps the tool catalog identical for cache stability; ui-plan chip and review tab; e2e plan-review.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already has a plan gate (ChatMessages.plan-gate.test.tsx); the explicit statement that plan mode is not enforcement is worth copying into its UI copy.

name: Scheduled tasks visible across surfaces, off by default in Desktop
what: Tasks are managed from an Automation tasks page and right-sidebar tab (search, filter, edit name, instruction and run time, browse records, delete, open the original conversation); an open session header shows a reminder clock, a schedule_create call renders a card, and quitting warns that scheduled tasks will not run while the app is closed.
how: schedule family (schedule_create, list, update, delete); ui-schedule with draft-and-save bar; armed reminders reported through workspace/session-activity; reminders fire only in loaded sessions; Desktop does not enable scheduled tasks by default.
verevonRelevance: Verevon ScheduledRunsPanel and ScheduleDialog exist; the cross-surface visibility and the warn-on-quit idea are the extras.

name: Background jobs panel with streamed output and completion notices
what: A session-header control lists background jobs with lifecycle, elapsed time and progress; live jobs and settled jobs with retained output expand to streaming panels, and finished jobs wake an idle agent or reach a busy agent at its next step.
how: tool-jobs (job_list, job_output, job_kill) over ctx.jobs; ui-jobs shows running and finished sections; collapsing stops the stream; configuration controls wait limits, completion delivery and an optional cap on consecutive wakeups.
verevonRelevance: Long-running agent tasks in Verevon (fleet runs, ingestion) deserve the same live output and elapsed-time panel.

name: Parallel tool-call cap as a user-visible setting
what: Plugins page Agent loop sets how many parallel-safe tool calls one step may run at once (default 10); exclusive calls keep ordering; the page marks overridden values and resets to the deployment default.
how: maxParallelToolCalls on dsh-agent-loop (DEFAULT_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS) edited through ui-settings-agent-loop with staged save.
verevonRelevance: Parallel dispatch was already adopted in Verevon (adoption plan 7.2); exposing the cap as a visible, resettable setting is optional.

name: Ignorable flag: unknown required events refuse to load
what: A reader that meets an unrecognised event type without the ignorable marker must refuse to reconstruct the session rather than silently dropping it, so a log written by a newer build is never half-interpreted; writers mark only purely informational records ignorable.
how: SessionEvent.ignorable?: true envelope field; KNOWN_SESSION_EVENT_TYPES (60 types) is generated and the persistence read path refuses outside types; event-name registration was rejected because it would make reads composition-dependent.
verevonRelevance: Event or run records in Model Plane should declare per-event whether older readers may skip them; this protects audit integrity across versions.

name: Adjacent session-format migrations that never overwrite committed generations
what: Session logs are versioned files (session.vN.jsonl); a migration adds a successor beside the source and never moves, overwrites or deletes committed generations; reads migrate in memory, writes publish the new version exclusively; persistence type changes require acknowledgement.
how: session-format-v0-to-v1 ... v3-to-v4 packages each own one step; header-only stat and list pick the highest canonical generation; a stored-session open refuses a future version; verify-persistence-* gates and persistence-changes records.
verevonRelevance: Run-event storage in Model Plane should keep old generations immutable and migrate adjacent versions so past audits stay reproducible.
notes: Pre-stable APIs: AGENTS.md says compatibility breaks are expected before stable.

name: Projection seam: typed whole-log state without replaying raw events
what: Registered projection units fold committed events incrementally so clients read current todos, goals, statistics, outlines and token usage as schema-validated JSON values paired with the last event reflected, with checkpoints for faster cold reads and host-only projections kept private.
how: ctx.sessionProjections registry (stateOf, snapshot with cropped client views); units for sessionStats, tokenUsage, contextPressure, contextBreakdown, turnOutline, turnBoundary; projection cache domain checkpoints every 200 events or 5 s; a host reader fails loudly if the registry is absent.
verevonRelevance: Verevon keyed-channel projection (src/shared/projection) is the client half; a server-side projection registry for stats, usage and outline is the missing half.
notes: Prior Verevon analysis already adopted a keyed projection channel; the registry and checkpointing are the additional detail.

name: Live configuration apply: validate, then persist, then HMR
what: Config edits from forms or the YAML file apply to the running process without restart: the editor validates the complete candidate before touching disk, serialises with profile changes and HMR, refuses writes a higher layer would override, and reloads plugins whose config changed.
how: config-editor persists through the active profile patch; dsh-hmr reloads plugin source and configuration with one queue (package installs run outside); .volatile() Config fields are the only form-editable ones; credentials re-resolve per operation.
verevonRelevance: Hot-applied, validated policy changes with refusal on layered overrides suit Verevon router-policy and org settings.

name: Customisation policy: no hardcoded tunables, explicit defaults, fail loud
what: Repository rules require deployment-varying choices to be validated Config fields editable from cordis.yml, defaults to be applied in one explicit resolve(request): Spec step rather than hidden fallbacks, and misconfiguration to fail at load; protocol constants and security invariants stay fixed.
how: AGENTS.md conventions: No hardcoded tunables in plugins; Explicit over implicit at package boundaries; Misconfiguration fails loud; generated config catalog cross-checks every schema key against the declaration; settings forms show only volatile fields.
verevonRelevance: Verevon planes could adopt the rule that every tunable is a declared, documented config field with a generated catalog.

name: Fork lineage recorded in the log with an inherited-prefix marker
what: Branching a conversation at a message creates a child session whose header records its parent and whether it contains an inherited prefix, with a session/end-seed marker at the exact cut so inherited history can be told apart from the child own work.
how: SessionHeader parentSession and isSeeded; session/end-seed {inherited} marker appended by the Session constructor or buildForkSeed; open turns at the cut close with turn/end forked; Chat exposes Branch into a new conversation (forkAt) and e2e covers fork-mid-turn.
verevonRelevance: Verevon chat-thread versions exist (chat-versions.ts); recording lineage and the exact inherited cut would make branches auditable.
notes: No edit-and-resend or regenerate of a sent message was found; branching is the only history-rewrite action.

name: Manual titles pin against automatic regeneration; title generation is configurable
what: Renaming a session sets an explicit title that automatic title generation will not replace; automatic titles come from a first-prompt LLM provider with word, character and byte limits and a timeout, falling back to a deterministic title.
how: session-title service with fallbackMaxWords 5, fallbackMaxBytes 40, maxTitleBytes 80; session-title-llm targetWords 5, targetCjkCharacters 10, maxInputBytes 4096, maxOutputTokens 4096, timeoutMs 60000; rename(title) pins; durable title snapshots.
verevonRelevance: Small, but pinning user-edited titles and exposing generation limits avoids surprising renames in Verevon thread lists.
notes: Rename contract (explicit user title pins against automatic regeneration) read in session.ts.

name: Legacy settings are imported once, renamed and never silently dropped
what: A settings.yaml left by earlier releases is imported once into the matching plugin entries of the active profile, then renamed to settings.yaml.imported before the first write; a section the running composition rejects is logged and survives only in the renamed file.
how: dsh-settings runs the import after the Loader has settled every entry; section ids are mapped to entries (ui-developer-tools to ui-settings, ui-onboarding to ui-settings-general, shell to the platform shell executor); the rename happens before the first write so an import cannot repeat.
verevonRelevance: When Verevon changes settings schemas, a one-shot import with a retained original and a log of rejected sections avoids silent loss of user choices.

name: Support questionnaire prefill is minimised and hidden from editing
what: The account menu Feedback entry opens an external questionnaire prefilled only with account UID (when the profile loaded), build version and a device_info string, each marked hidden; tokens and masked contacts are never included, stale prefill values are dropped first and a configured form URL cannot re-add removed fields.
how: Context is sampled at each click; each field also carries a hide_*=1 parameter; os_version, device_brand, app_locale and separate screen_resolution parameters are removed; the Desktop bridge supplies deviceInfo (physical screen resolution after devicePixelRatio rounding) and falls back to navigator.userAgent; contactFormUrl is configurable and must be HTTPS.
verevonRelevance: Support and feedback links in Verevon should state and constrain exactly which identifiers are prefilled, sampled at click time.
notes: Third-party questionnaire host (Feishu); the README documents the data it receives.

name: Broken bundles stay visible with an error and can be deselected
what: A selected bundle that cannot load remains in the Plugins list with its error, the page lets the user deselect it, a broken bundle cannot be enabled, and the management bundles stay protected if their files become unreadable.
how: listBundles reports enabled (saved selection) separately from load success; a not-bundle problem is reported for a selected package without a bundle patch; unselected plain dependencies are not listed; installed copies and on-demand catalog entries carry availability and installTarget.
verevonRelevance: Verevon integrations and agent installs should show a failed state with a reason and a remove action instead of failing the whole page.
notes: Whether the full boot degrades per plugin was not verified here; the prior Verevon analysis claimed boot is all-or-nothing.

name: Bilingual documentation pairs with hash-checked consistency records
what: Every in-scope document exists in English and Simplified Chinese with equal authority, and a per-heading hash record fails CI when one side changes without the other, so users and agents get the same facts in both languages.
how: foo.md, foo.zh.md and foo.i18n.yaml per document; the record holds an English and a Chinese hash per heading section outside code and generated regions; verify-translation-pairing --write re-records after editing; terminology and translation rules are single sources.
verevonRelevance: Verevon ships Norwegian and English; a pairing record would keep policy and privacy pages from diverging between locales.

name: Namespaced plugin records keep experimental log writes outside the closed event vocabulary
what: Experimental packages write their own session log records under a plugin: type prefix; these are never members of the core event map or released schemas, the owner must validate data on read because an older build may have written it, and format migrations can rename such events into the namespace.
how: PluginRecordType is a template literal type plugin:segment/segment; PluginRecordMap is augmented by packages to type writes; pluginRecordOf reads committed PluginRecord {type, seq, time, data}; a verify-plugin-record-callers gate exists in the root scripts.
verevonRelevance: A reserved namespace for experimental or tenant-specific run records lets Verevon trial new audit fields without widening the audited core vocabulary.
notes: package.json:150 is the verify-plugin-record-callers script; the gate itself was not opened.

name: Desktop product analytics: default-on with no user-facing control
what: The Desktop build reports selected UI interaction events (launch, sign-in clicks, send, model and effort switches, plugin toggles, forks) to a vendor OTLP collector by default; Settings has no control for it, ordinary Web never mounts it, and disabling it only stops new events.
how: dsh-client-product-analytics declares Config.enabled as a volatile boolean defaulting to true with the comment 'no user settings surface'; the web-app bundle patch mounts it together with dsh-host-product-telemetry-otel only when profileContext.name is desktop; the exporter defaults to a deepseeksvc.com collector (override DSH_PRODUCT_ANALYTICS_OTLP_URL); Desktop re-reads the policy at event intake and after identity lookup; the README states there is no user-facing control and that disabling does not clear the exporter queue.
verevonRelevance: Verevon must propagate Zero-Data-Retention and org privacy posture to analytics as well as content; this is the anti-pattern to avoid, a vendor-bound channel with no user or admin switch.
notes: Contrast with feedback-only session telemetry (separate record), which has a Settings switch or DSH_TELEMETRY_DISABLED. The earlier inventory listed telemetry channels but not this third channel. Delivery is best effort with no durable outbox.

name: Typed product-event vocabulary as the analytics privacy boundary
what: Every analytics event name and attribute set is a compile-time declaration, and the README states that prompts, responses, API keys and account tokens are never event fields; plugin-install inputs keep only registry identifiers and plain versions (Git sources become a placeholder).
how: ProductEventMap in events.ts declares 22 events (desktop_app_launch, auth_page_click, send_button_click with msg_type default|queue|steer and run_mode plan|goal|default, model_switch, thinking_level_switch, context_compression, branch_session_click, plugin_toggle, install_plugin_result and others); ProductEvent is a discriminated union; common fields are device_id, user_id, os_version, app_version read credential-free through deepseekAccount.getDeviceIdentity(); message events are captured before async command adjudication so claimed commands are excluded; capture failures cannot interrupt submission; the exporter reads no Session, account or device identifier itself.
verevonRelevance: A closed event enum is a cheap, reviewable privacy guardrail; Verevon could mirror it as a Rust enum so analytics fields cannot grow without a code review and a ZDR check.
notes: device_id and user_id are still collected, so the channel is identified, not anonymous (unlike the anonymous install id used for feedback telemetry).

name: OpenTelemetry is logs-only: no trace spans or user-owned trace export
what: The harness's OpenTelemetry support exports log-record events only (product events and feedback-released session-log prefixes) to deployer-configured collectors; there are no spans, no GenAI semantic conventions and no user-facing trace export, so users inspect behaviour solely through the local Trajectory view and session log.
how: packages/telemetry/otel depends on @opentelemetry/api-logs and sdk-logs and exposes createEventReporter and a session-log channel with independent queues; docs say mounting the service allocates no provider or transport; a keyword sweep of packages/ and apps/ for startSpan, getTracer and gen_ai found no tracing use; DSH_TELEMETRY_OTLP_URL and DSH_PRODUCT_ANALYTICS_OTLP_URL only redirect the destination.
verevonRelevance: Verevon can leapfrog this gap by emitting OTel GenAI spans per run, step and tool call for tenant observability while keeping ZDR redaction at the exporter.
notes: Negative finding from a keyword sweep; spans could exist in a path the sweep missed, hence medium confidence. Local-first inspection (Trajectory) is strong; operator-grade tracing is absent.

name: Headless one-shot separates live reasoning (stderr) from the answer (stdout)
what: dsh --profile headless streams each non-empty reasoning delta to stderr under a dsh: reasoning: heading and prints only the final assistant text on stdout, exiting 0 only when the final turn ended as completed, so scripts get a clean answer and a live trace.
how: headless-runner observes agent/assistant-stream for the exact agent it creates after startup quiescence, writes the heading once, flushes the session, then derives the last non-empty assistant text and final turn/end reason from the durable interval; a built-bin e2e test pins the exact stderr string.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's API and agent run endpoints should expose reasoning as a separable stream channel and map turn end reasons to machine-readable status codes.
notes: A decision note (2026-08-21 headless reasoning progress) is archived and frozen; the README and code are the current truth.

name: Server-driven mandatory update block in Desktop
what: Desktop polls a vendor policy endpoint; when it answers error code 40005 a shell-owned modal blocks further plugin changes until the user updates, showing server-supplied title and detail and an allowlisted download page with a copy-address fallback, while already-running tasks keep running.
how: DesktopMandatoryUpdatePolicy polls /api/v0/check_client_update (default interval 600000 ms, jitter 0.2, back-off to 1 h); parsePolicy treats code 40005 as blocking and any other shape as an error; desktopPolicyPage accepts only HTTPS URLs whose origin is in allowedPageOrigins; the policy is embedded at packaging and packaged apps ignore runtime overrides; only a fresh valid no-force response clears the block and authentication failure never does.
verevonRelevance: A minimum-client-version gate is useful for Verevon desktop or agent clients, but it removes user control; Verevon should make such blocks explainable and non-destructive as DSH does.
notes: Automatic checks never open dialogs or download packages; a user-initiated download needs a separate install confirmation, but a mandatory policy overrides that choice. Test builds use a Feishu-gated login window (internal).

name: Update checks disclose a fixed, documented client fingerprint
what: Update and Platform API requests carry platform, architecture, client version, bundled dsh version, locale, UTC offset and the fixed Nightly channel plus an intentionally empty bundle id, and use no business login credentials or installation id.
how: The Desktop host sends the same Platform client headers for account and update-policy requests; the policy request adds architecture, update channel and bundled runtime version; the README enumerates every field so the disclosure is auditable.
verevonRelevance: Documenting the exact outbound client metadata per request class is a good transparency habit for Verevon's desktop and browser agents.
notes: Disclosure exists in developer docs, not in the in-app UI.

name: Desktop-local settings file independent of Host configuration
what: The Electron shell reads userData/desktop/settings.json once at startup, independently of the Host and Cordis config, creating it if absent, never overwriting, preserving unknown fields and falling back to defaults on any read or validation failure.
how: Today the document holds only updates.allowTestAuthPopupWindow (default false); DSH_HOME does not relocate it; installation updates retain it and Windows uninstall removes it; an architecture decision note defines Host-independent ownership and migration criteria.
verevonRelevance: Shell-level settings that must work before the backend boots should live outside tenant configuration; relevant if Verevon ships a desktop wrapper.
notes: Only one field exists today, so the pattern is more a boundary decision than a feature.

name: DevTools toggle shortcut works in packaged Desktop builds
what: F12 (Fn+F12), Command+Option+I or Ctrl+Shift+I toggles DevTools for the focused application page even in packaged builds, while update overlays and packaged embedded-browser guests disable DevTools.
how: Hidden application-menu items carry the native shortcuts; DevTools is deliberately disabled for update overlays and embedded guests so the mandatory-update surface cannot be inspected or tampered with through it.
verevonRelevance: Low cost way to let power users and support inspect the frontend; Verevon web already has browser DevTools, so relevant mainly to any desktop shell.
notes: Test-login windows open detached DevTools with F12 for diagnosis.

name: Optional dsh command registration from the Desktop menu
what: Manage dsh Command offers Install, Repair and Remove for a dsh terminal command that uses the app's bundled runtime and works with the app closed; it reports PATH precedence conflicts and asks for confirmation before replacing an existing command.
how: macOS creates /usr/local/bin/dsh with administrator authentication and preserves and restores a displaced launcher; Windows registers the user PATH and preserves other entries; shell startup files are never edited; the uninstaller does not remove the registration, so Remove must run first.
verevonRelevance: If Verevon ships a local agent or CLI companion, a reversible, explicit PATH registration with conflict reporting is a user-respecting install pattern.
notes: Uninstall asymmetry (registration survives uninstall) is a documented limitation.

name: Close-to-background with a one-time acknowledgement and tray access
what: Closing the Desktop window hides it while agents and jobs keep running; Windows asks once and keeps a tray icon with Open and Quit; reopening restores the same document with session, drafts and scroll position.
how: Close hides rather than destroys the window; the acknowledgement is recorded as a background-close-confirmed marker under Electron userData (Escape or dialog failure records nothing); the page and Host keep running; macOS returns through the Dock, a second launch or a dsh://open URL; every real quit asks the Host what would be interrupted.
verevonRelevance: Agent products with long-running work need explicit close-versus-quit semantics; Verevon's desktop or PWA shell should state whether work continues.
notes: Complements the quit-warning record, which covers the interruption check itself.

name: Upgrade guides as a gated artifact for every externally visible break
what: Each breaking change to a CLI flag, profile, config key, persisted data format, SDK or wire message ships a short Change plus Migration guide in the same PR, with ordered steps and a check that confirms the migration worked.
how: docs/upgrade-guide/v<version>/<item>/guide.md with exact frontmatter (kind and one-sentence description), the two required sections, at most 500 words, a Chinese twin and a pairing record; verify-upgrade-guides runs in the quick gate set; older version directories freeze at the version bump; a repository skill (dsh-create-upgrade-guide) tells agents when and how to write one.
verevonRelevance: CoresSystem has stale-doc registers and many cross-plane contracts; a per-break guide with a verification command, enforced by a CI gate like the existing generated-doc checks, would give operators reliable upgrade notes.
notes: 25 guides across three pre-release versions (2 in v0.1.7-rc.2, 5 in v0.2.0-rc.2, 18 in v0.2.1-alpha.1), counted from the directory listing.

name: Claude Code mods bridge: run mod hooks inside agent runs
what: An alpha bridge lets a Claude Code mod (hooks that guard tool calls, rewrite prompts, add commands and tools, read session facts and draw a band above the prompt) run in a DSH session, wrapped with defineMod and mounted as an ordinary plugin; unserved events are named in a warning at load.
how: defineMod({name,version,root,userConfig,register}) returns a Cordis plugin whose config overlays the userConfig defaults; the engine runs hooks through one $, e, next chain; bridge config includes hookTimeoutMs 10000, catchTimeoutMs 1000, processTimeoutMs 30000, toolAliases (Claude Code tool name to harness tool name), bandColumns 120 and bandRows 10; tool.call hooks run around tools/execute after the harness permission decision; a compatibility page lists every difference from Claude Code 2.1.287.
verevonRelevance: Compatibility with Claude Code's extension model is a path to reuse community mods; Verevon could expose a similar hook chain (guard, rewrite, render) as a governed plugin surface.
notes: Experimental and off by default; the mods feature itself is described by Anthropic documentation that was not read here, so the comparison rests on the bridge's own compatibility table (DOC).

name: Mod-drawn status and action band above the composer
what: A mod's ui.render hook can return a Box/Text/Button tree that the Web client draws as a full-width band above the prompt, with buttons that run the mod's onPress on the Host and redraw; while a press is in flight all buttons disable and refusals show under the band.
how: client-ui-claude-code-mods mounts the bridge's claudeCodeMods Remote, watches each open session's band, renders the serialized tree using Claude Code's terminal palette on the theme tokens; only the AbovePrompt render site is served; one band per session; Host renders for 120 columns and the web band wraps.
verevonRelevance: A plugin-owned, serializable UI region next to the composer (status, forecast, confirm buttons) is a safer extension seam than arbitrary component injection for Verevon's SolidJS client.
notes: No panes, text inputs, hotkeys or focus; mod UI is a declarative tree, not code running in the browser.

name: Token Weather: live context-window forecast mod
what: A ready-made mod keeps a 12-reading history of context use and draws a one-line forecast (Clear, Cloudy, Showers, Storm, Compact soon) with percent of window, tokens used and a sparkline above the prompt after each main-loop turn.
how: Hooks on session.start and turn.complete call $.session.usage() for context tokens, window and percent; readings persist through $.state (so a hot reload keeps history); ui.render for AbovePrompt returns the band using bars from the character ramp and thresholds 25, 50, 75 and 90 percent; subagent turns are ignored.
verevonRelevance: A glanceable context-pressure indicator that warns before compaction fits Verevon's chat page and complements a per-run token meter.
notes: Module is the published example from Anthropic's mods post, reproduced unchanged in the repo (stated in its header comment).

name: Blast Radius: preview and hold risky shell commands behind Proceed or Cancel
what: A mod classifies Bash commands (recursive delete, git reset --hard, git clean, force-push, database migrations), measures what they would touch, shows the report in a pane or the band and holds the command until the user presses Proceed or Cancel; Cancel returns a denial the model sees.
how: tool.call hook with tool Bash matches RISKS regexes, runs read-only measurement commands (git status, git clean -n, du), opens a ui pane or falls back to the band, then polls with $.process.run so waiting does not consume the hook's time budget; the DSH wrapper supplies a portable Node timer for Windows.
verevonRelevance: Approval cards that show a computed impact report (what would be deleted) are stronger than a bare command string; Verevon's computer-use and sandbox approvals could include dry-run impact.
notes: Regex classification is illustrative, not a security boundary; the completed parts of the module were written by the repo authors from the post's description (its header says so).

name: Replay Theater: step through the last turn's edits one diff at a time
what: A mod records Edit and Write tool calls during a turn, registers a /replay command and shows each edit as a stepped diff in a pane (or inline in the band when no pane can be placed), one replay per completed turn.
how: tool.call hook collects old and new text into pending steps; turn.complete seals them into replay for main-loop turns; session.start registers the command through $.command.register; command.run replies Replaying or No edits; ui.render serves a Pane or AbovePrompt tree.
verevonRelevance: Reviewing an agent's edits as a guided sequence is a good transparency pattern for Verevon's agent pages when documents or files change.
notes: Complements DSH's native per-turn changed-files card, which lists files rather than replaying steps.

name: Mods and bridge hooks run with the full authority of the harness process
what: Claude Code mods loaded through the bridge are not sandboxed: the hooks module runs in-process with Node globals, and $.env, $.http.fetch, $.fs and $.tool.call act with the session's and process's authority; the docs say to mount only mods you would run as a plugin.
how: Compatibility table row on mod access: Claude Code mods reach the host only through $, DSH applies no access rule; every mod loads as tier user; managed tiers are not a DSH concept; next.to rejects.
verevonRelevance: Any Verevon plugin hook surface must decide up front whether hooks are sandboxed per tenant; DSH's candid trust statement is the minimum disclosure.
notes: Consistent with the repository-wide stance that plugin installation is gated like Full access.

name: User-owned sidebar terminals separate from the agent
what: The right sidebar opens real shell tabs in the session's working directory that the user types into; they survive reloads and sidebar collapse, can be renamed, show exit codes, and their output never enters the agent transcript.
how: terminal-controller exposes remote.terminal (environment, shells, list, create, retain, follow, write, resize, rename, close) per Session; defaults maxTerminals 8, scrollback 1000, maxBufferedBytes 2 MiB, maxInputBytes 64 KiB, candidate shells zsh, bash, fish, pwsh, powershell, cmd; Take control makes an attachment writable when another page owns input; exited shells never restart automatically; processes are closed as complete provider-owned process ranges; terminal commands run with the system user's permissions independent of agent permissions.
verevonRelevance: A user terminal beside the agent, explicitly outside agent context and agent permissions, is a clean model for Verevon's sandbox pages; processes do not survive Host restart, which Verevon's sandboxes should improve on.
notes: Limits: bounded history, no split panes, no restore after Host restart, no completion engine of its own. The user terminal bypasses the agent sandbox by design, which the docs say plainly.

name: Sidebar browser with a default iframe sandbox and a link-destination preference
what: HTTP(S) pages, including loopback services, open in independent right-sidebar tabs; Settings chooses whether chat links open in the in-app browser or the external browser; the browser is off by default in Web profiles and on in Desktop, and its sandbox limits are spelled out.
how: Web uses an iframe with application-managed history; Desktop uses an Electron webview with native history; the package never injects Electron or Node access into visited content; hosts without a scheme become HTTPS; ui-chat.linkOpening stores In-App Sidebar (default) or Default Browser and is shown only while the browser plugin is registered; the sandbox can be disabled for compatibility at the cost of top-level navigation, downloads, modals and input locks.
verevonRelevance: An in-app browser tab beside the chat is the user-side mirror of Verevon's browser grants; its documented iframe limits (X-Frame-Options, mixed content, invisible cross-origin URLs) show why a real remote browser is needed for agent use.
notes: This is a user browsing aid, not agent browser control; the agent's browser use is a separate experimental seam.

name: HTML preview with static sanitized mode and scripted sandbox mode
what: HTML files open in the sidebar either as a sanitized static document (no scripts, no external resources) or, when Coding Tools is on, as a live preview in an iframe that may run scripts but cannot reach the parent origin; related local scripts and stylesheets are packed within fixed limits.
how: Off: DOMPurify-sanitized document in an iframe with no sandbox permissions plus CSP blocking scripts, external resources, connections, forms and nested frames; hrefs, refresh directives and declarative shadow roots removed. On: Blob iframe with exactly sandbox allow-scripts and no allow-same-origin; direct classic .js and .css references are read through the Host (4 MiB per asset, 32 MiB total, 64 assets); both modes name the frame dsh-sidebar-html-<tab-id>.
verevonRelevance: Verevon already renders generated HTML in a srcdoc iframe with allow-scripts and no same-origin; the addition worth taking is the inert, sanitized default tier (CSP, no scripts) for untrusted or ZDR-sensitive artifacts.
notes: The mode is tied to a developer-feature switch (Coding Tools), not to a per-file trust decision.

name: Pluggable document preview: paged text, PDF, images, spreadsheets and local Office conversion
what: The right sidebar previews workspace files with a renderer dropdown, wrap toggle and automatic or manual reload: Markdown and code load in pages, PDF, HTML, images and spreadsheets load as complete bytes, Word and PowerPoint convert locally to PDF, and unknown extensions fall back to plain text.
how: ctx.documentPreviews.register({id, extensions, binaryExtensions, priority, title, loading, wrap}) plus a keyed body slot; loading modes text-pages, bytes-complete and renderer; the Host maxFileBytes cap rejects oversize files instead of truncating; reload tracks a ResourceGroup of dependencies; PDF raster allocation is capped at 16,777,216 pixels per page; a sibling file-tree tab lists the workspace root with direct-entry watches (listing only, one root).
verevonRelevance: Verevon artifact and file previews can follow the registry-by-extension design with explicit loading modes and size caps instead of per-format special cases.
notes: Preview only: no editing, no shared search. Office conversion fidelity belongs to the LibreOffice provider; spreadsheets use fortune-sheet in the browser.

name: Workspace and session manager with folded history and pending indicators
what: The sidebar lists grouped or flat sessions per workspace; five idle sessions show by default with Show more, running sessions always stay visible, warning dots mark pending interactions, a clock mark and hover card show scheduled tasks, and sessions can be renamed, reordered, searched, forked and archived but never deleted.
how: ui-workspace owns row and hover-button slot lists that plugins extend; canonically distinct paths stay separate workspaces; adding a workspace needs a composed directory picker (native or in-app browse); subagent-origin sessions are hidden; content search is literal token or phrase matching and a result opens the session, not the event.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's thread list is capped at 80 with no paging and projects are a browser-only organizer; DSH's folded per-workspace lists with running sessions pinned and pending-interaction dots are a usable model, though its archive-only stance must be reconciled with ZDR erasure.
notes: Pending interactions in collapsed groups do not light the group header (documented limitation).

name: Unified slash and at-mention menu with atomic file, folder and session references
what: Typing / or @ opens one grouped completion menu: commands, then files and folders, then sessions; picks insert atomic references with a stable clipboard form, folder rows let users descend, and session mentions are validated before any model context is captured.
how: ui-input-trigger provides the grouped menu and keyboard or pointer selection over registered sources; ui-reference supplies file and session sources through Host ctx.fileReferences and ctx.sessionReferenceResolver; the reference is plain draft text (a hand-typed identical token is the same reference); candidate failures are quiet; session search covers id, cwd and latest title only, not transcripts.
verevonRelevance: Verevon has no server-side conversation search or Data Plane mention menu in chat; a single trigger pipeline with pluggable sources (documents, spaces, threads) fits the composer without growing a central switch.
notes: A session-reference preparation failure occurs after prompt acceptance and ends the turn (documented limitation).

name: Skill invocation by /name with host-command precedence and a stable Instructions card
what: A skill is invoked by picking it from the slash menu or typing /name; a name shared with a host command resolves to the command; the call appears as an expandable Instructions card whose settled contents do not change when the installed catalog later changes.
how: ui-skill registers a skill source for the trigger menu and a keyed tool presentation; command adjudication claims the line client-side before it becomes a prompt; the sent message carries the literal text and the host loads the skill identically for menu picks and hand-typed tokens across Web, TUI and ACP; the menu prewarms the catalog cache.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's skills live behind Model Plane routes; a deterministic rule that host commands win over same-named skills, plus a frozen record of the instructions that ran, would make skill use auditable in chat.
notes: Known limits: result-only history pages fall back to a generic row; a menu opened before prewarm settles shows no skills for that keystroke.

name: Attachment draft rail, drop overlay and image lightbox
what: Attachments appear in one ordered draft rail under the composer with upload controls, a full-viewport drop invitation that states the limits, durable images in chat, trajectory and tool results, and a lightbox for the original image.
how: ui-attachment registers into slots declared by ui-conversation and ui-tool; data, upload state and image loading come from the slot owners; images are sized by count; the lightbox closes on Escape, mask or close button but offers no zoom or download and does not trap focus.
verevonRelevance: Standard multimodal input affordance; the explicit limits line on the drop overlay is a small honesty detail worth copying.
notes: Lightbox accessibility gaps (no focus trap) are acknowledged.

name: Deterministic web-search provider seam with honest per-provider limits
what: web_search resolves to a named provider (DeepSeek native search, Exa, Perplexity) by an explicit searchProvider id or, if exactly one is usable, automatically; zero or several usable providers produce a named error, never a hidden priority chain; each provider documents what it cannot do.
how: WebRuntime selection semantics: configured and available wins, configured but missing is WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_MISSING, configured but unavailable is WEB_PROVIDER_CONFIGURED_UNAVAILABLE, none configured with several usable is WEB_PROVIDER_AMBIGUOUS; DSH_WEB_SEARCH_PROVIDER feeds the same field; Exa returns no answer text and drops results without a highlight, Perplexity returns a generated answer and cannot cap results on the wire, DeepSeek search costs a full model turn; a Plugins-page card edits key, endpoint and per-request search budget with Overridden badges and writes the key through the credentials domain.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's research capability needs a provider abstraction with predictable selection and visible cost; the per-provider limitation tables are a model for honest capability disclosure.
notes: Only three provider-specific knobs are exposed per provider; domain filters, recency and livecrawl wait on provider-neutral fields (documented).

name: Local push-to-record voice input with integrity-pinned model downloads
what: An opt-in voice bundle adds a microphone button that records, shows live levels, and transcribes into the draft on-device with SenseVoice and Silero VAD; models are downloaded only after the user starts preparation, from a user-selectable origin, with hashes verified.
how: speech-to-text-sensevoice runs sherpa-onnx on CPU (INT8 about 239 MB, FP32 about 938 MB); revision-pinned files are verified by size and SHA-256 before load; origins default to Hugging Face and HF-Mirror, are probed with concurrent HEAD requests, and the UI offers Automatic or a manual source for that task only; the input-device selector never silently falls back; recordings and preparation stay outside model requests; Desktop restricts microphone access to the primary app frame.
verevonRelevance: Privacy-preserving on-device STT with disclosed downloads is a differentiator versus cloud-only voice; Verevon could offer it as a local-mode option under ZDR.
notes: Experimental, CPU only, native packages for macOS arm64/x64, Linux glibc and Windows x64; an api-speech-to-text package also exists (not read) for remote STT.

name: Opt-in tmux location context appended only when it changes
what: When the agent runs inside tmux, an opt-in plugin tells the model which session, window and pane (and pane-tree layout) it occupies, as one sourced message on the first step of a turn, and only when the location changed.
how: Durable user-role context message; detection requires the process's controlling tty to match $TMUX_PANE's pane_tty so inherited variables in editor terminals add nothing; never captures sibling pane text; failed queries add nothing and do not fail the turn; not in shipped Web or headless profiles.
verevonRelevance: Low direct relevance; the change-only, sourced, durable context pattern generalises to environment facts Verevon feeds the model.
notes: Same pattern as the clock-reading context record: changing facts appended only when they change.

name: Manual /compact command with a saved-tokens report
what: Typing /compact condenses older history into one summary on demand without spending a model turn and reports how many history items were condensed and the estimated tokens saved; it refuses while a turn or condensation is already running.
how: dsh-command-compact registers a command over the compaction seam and works with any backend; prompts sent meanwhile queue and start afterwards; no range or policy arguments (programmatic compactRegion covers ranges); surfaces without ctx.commands rely on automatic pressure compaction; Desktop analytics counts manual and auto triggers separately.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's Model Plane has compaction but no user-visible manual control or savings report in chat; exposing it as a run command with a tokens-saved result fits the SSE event taxonomy.
notes: The command is idle-only by design.

name: Open In split button for the workspace and previewed files
what: A session-header split button opens the workspace directory in the remembered local application, its chevron lists installed catalog applications, and the document preview gains Open and Show file location buttons when the Host has a desktop.
how: dsh-host-open-in-app probes the application catalog and owns launches; the browser package renders controls only if at least one app is installed and the workspace is known; path verification runs through the composed filesystem so unmapped paths never launch; availability is read once per page; catalog entries missing locale strings stay hidden rather than showing raw ids.
verevonRelevance: Relevant only to local or desktop deployments; a cloud Verevon would instead download or sync artifacts.
notes: One reveal label for all platforms because the host reports only whether a desktop exists.

name: Assistant file links open previews with line anchors and image hover thumbnails
what: Markdown file links in assistant messages open in the right sidebar after the message settles, honour #L24 and #L24-L30 line fragments, reuse an existing file tab, and show a thumbnail on hover or keyboard focus for image links; sent file references and confirmed skills also open there.
how: ui-chat supplies a MarkdownDelegateProvider with openFile and openExternalLink; relative paths resolve in the viewed session's workspace and absolute paths keep that session's filesystem access; only the decoded path and first line reach the opener, URL schemes, queries and malformed destinations never do; missing files show the preview error state; sessions, directories and command labels stay non-navigating.
verevonRelevance: Verevon answers that cite documents or generated files should link to previews with anchors; the sanitizing opener contract is reusable.
notes: Link hover uses the shared HoverCard inline mode with Escape dismissal.

name: Chat hides system and context rows while Trajectory remains the complete view
what: Chat omits the system prompt, ordinary context injections and permission command rows in every work-details mode, but the Trajectory tab and the session log still show them; non-human turn triggers stay visible as bordered notices and tool-changing context stays visible.
how: A display filter in ui-chat changes neither recorded events nor Trajectory inspection; retired assistant attempts without visible content hide their published node but keep its key so a retry reuses it; Trajectory shows a system row even when only the appended prompt is loaded, without inventing options or a tool catalog.
verevonRelevance: A two-surface disclosure design (clean chat for reading, exhaustive trajectory for auditing) is a good pattern for Verevon chat versus run-inspector pages.
notes: The completeness of Trajectory depends on the whole-log projections; paged windows can leave a prompt unavailable until its page loads.

name: Incremental streaming Markdown renderer with resumable syntax highlighting
what: While a reply streams, only the trailing blocks re-parse per chunk and completed blocks stay frozen, and an open code fence is highlighted from saved grammar state line by line, so long answers stay responsive; the settled full parse resolves references that crossed the freeze boundary.
how: MarkdownText freezes all but the trailing two blocks as cached React elements; an unclosed top-level fence keeps its parsed node and sends only the last completed and partial lines through the GFM grammar; Shiki grammar state resumes per fence; CodeBlock seals completed lines in fixed-size React groups; lines of 1,000 or more UTF-16 units render uncolored to avoid superlinear TextMate cost.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's chat baseline lists no virtualization and a full re-parse per streamed token as a known gap, so freezing completed blocks and resuming highlight state directly addresses a documented Frontend Plane weakness.
notes: Known limits: reference-style links and footnotes across the freeze boundary render literally until settle; a long highlighted fence keeps its full token DOM.

name: Untrusted GFM and TeX rendering with link, image and file-mention sanitisation
what: Assistant Markdown renders as untrusted GFM with TeX math, blocks unsafe links and images, turns resolved file mentions into explicit controls, and rewrites local image paths to displayable URLs only after the reply settles and only when the owner supplies a path vocabulary.
how: micromark parsing and KaTeX typesetting in ui-primitives; images accept HTTP(S), data, blob and the Desktop dsh-app file route, authored Desktop URLs stay inert; failed images show alt text or the destination; the compact variant used for thinking text keeps tables and math enabled with horizontal scroll; the parser recovers only complete, unescaped, standalone local image references.
verevonRelevance: Verevon needs the same untrusted-output rendering baseline (math, tables, code, safe links), and the settled-only local-path rewrite avoids flicker and spoofing while streaming.
notes: No Mermaid or chart rendering was found in this package.

name: Typed tool-result cards with head-plus-tail folding, ANSI handling and bounded line diffs
what: Tool results render as intent-specific cards (terminal, read, diff, search, web, JSON tree) that fold long bodies to head and tail behind an expand button, preserve column alignment, parse ANSI, and offer copy; diffs show real additions and deletions with up to three context lines.
how: TerminalBlock, ReadBlock, DiffBlock, SearchBlock, WebBlock and JsonTree share one geometry (white-space pre, horizontal scroll, maxLines default 16); DiffBlock stops precise alignment beyond 256 line additions or deletions per fragment and shows a coarse replacement; TerminalBlock honours SGR, carriage return, backspace, erase-in-line and tab stops but strips absolute cursor and alternate-screen sequences and is not a terminal emulator.
verevonRelevance: Verevon tool and run views can share a small set of typed result cards with explicit truncation honesty instead of free-form text dumps.
notes: Complements the tool-card record on preparing stage and truncation flags.

name: Local echoes of user input are replaced atomically by durable records
what: A submitted message or steering text appears immediately in chat and disappears in the same render when the authoritative session record arrives, so the transcript neither flickers nor duplicates; queued messages stay outside chat in the queue dock.
how: Local transcript and steering echoes stay mounted through inbox acceptance and claim; matching local echoes are used in place for cross-client inbox order; admitted local steering suppresses stale inbox rows until the claim projection arrives; after reconnect Host-owned rows replace receipt-confirmed echoes; the open-turn control and echoes share one keyed list so the control's arrival preserves echo identity.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's mid-run queue and resume paths (queued input, Last-Event-ID resume) need the same optimistic-then-authoritative reconciliation; DSH's keyed-echo rule avoids duplicate or flickering bubbles when a durable receipt arrives.
notes: A claim awaiting admission may briefly have no bubble after reconnect (documented).

name: Explicit file delivery plus links from inline-code mentions in closing prose
what: Beyond the changed-files card, the model can explicitly present files as delivery cards, and inline-code file mentions in the closing message become links that open in the sidebar; terminal-created files appear on the card once git sees them but need explicit delivery for a card or inline link.
how: ui-deliverables lists paths only from the recorded summary, successful mutations and explicit deliveries, never from the prose; mention matching uses exact paths, unique argument aliases or unique basenames; the tool-present package supplies the present tool; declarations do not preserve file contents so reopening a session needs the files to still exist; missing files, directories and final symlinks return 404.
verevonRelevance: Verevon artifacts are model-created and read-only in the UI; the DSH rule that cards derive from recorded facts, never from prose, is a safe basis for Output-panel links and for file receipts under ZDR.
notes: tool-present was not read directly beyond the UI package's description.

name: Documentation site serves raw Markdown twins and an llms.txt index
what: The VitePress documentation site is projected from the repository docs and also serves a plain Markdown twin of every route (URL plus .md) and a root llms.txt index, so agents and users can fetch machine-readable docs.
how: website/ owns only configuration and a publication manifest; docs.ts maps selected docs pages to routes; raw-markdown.ts answers llms.txt as text/plain and .md routes as text/markdown, derived from the manifest at build time; production builds refuse output paths that escape the site root; Copy actions fetch raw Markdown with a dsh-raw=1 query.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's own documentation and API reference should ship raw Markdown and llms.txt so customer agents can read them.
notes: Docs are bilingual with hash-checked pairing (separate record in this file).

name: Theme-owned token discipline enforced by specs
what: Feature components may use only semantic --dsw-alias-* tokens, shared controls come from one primitives catalog, menus use one theme-owned surface material, and elevation, hairline borders and corner shape follow rules that theme specs enforce in tests.
how: ui-theme owns the static scale, aliases, typography, motion and light or dark preference; docs/web-styling.md forbids Tailwind and component libraries, literal colors and theme selectors in feature CSS; the ui-theme specs reject unwrapped menu renderers, material overrides, wider neutral borders and missing corner-shape pairs; elevated surfaces use shadow tokens with a 0.5px hairline as the first shadow layer.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's SolidJS frontend can adopt token-only styling with test-enforced rules to keep a multi-team UI coherent.
notes: Rules reference ui-theme specs that were not run (read-only audit).

name: Repository-owned agent skills encode engineering process
what: The repo ships 16 skill entries under .agents/skills covering code review, error handling, client UI/UX, prose standard, documentation, upgrade guides, archiving decision notes, CI test reliability, performance work, pre-push checks and trimming leaked reasoning prose, so contributors' agents follow the same rules as humans.
how: Each skill is a SKILL.md with a trigger description; skills reference gates (verify-* scripts), templates and Agent Notes; the product also ships an agent-experience skill inside the agent-preset package, linked from here; dsh-error-handling states that untrusted state or unknown outcomes must be visible and never claim success or safe retry without guarantees.
verevonRelevance: Verevon's CoresSystem could encode plane-boundary, ZDR and review rules as repo skills so agent contributions respect them mechanically.
notes: dsh-trim-cot-leakage targets docs that read like a leaked reasoning transcript, an unusual hygiene rule.

name: Process permission fallback and platform-specific process visibility are documented
what: New sessions in base profiles default to workspace-write (writes confined to the workspace and temp roots, reads and network unrestricted), DSH_PERMISSION_MODE changes the process fallback, and the docs state that only bwrap hides host processes while Landlock and Seatbelt leave them visible; the sdk-minimal tree pins danger-full-access with no approval service.
how: Permission presets feed sandbox mode and approval policy together; stored General-settings permissions affect later Web sessions, not an open one; the CLI reference spells out which backend gives a private PID namespace; sdk-minimal mounts no approval or permission-settings service.
verevonRelevance: Verevon sandboxes should publish a per-backend matrix of what is and is not confined (filesystem, network, process visibility) rather than one generic claim.
notes: Complements the sandbox-enforcement-as-a-fact record by stating the residual exposure per platform.

name: Plugin-claimable quota notice with held notices
what: A quota or account-quota failure raises a frame-wide notice that outlives the chat panel; a plugin can claim it and keep it open with a release the claimant must run, otherwise a warning toast is used, and newer notices replace the current one unless held.
how: ui-chat registers an entry in shell.overlay that offers the live notice to the shell.quota-notice chain; keepOpen() returns an owned release; dismissal and sign-out clear all holds; only sessions the client has bound and materialized publish; the failure row in chat states neutral quota copy instead of the provider message and persists even if a toast timer elapses unseen.
verevonRelevance: Billing and quota failures are a first-class UX moment for Verevon; a claimable notice chain lets billing plugins present top-up flows without chat knowing about them.
notes: Desktop account views can cover the toast; the persistent row is the durable fallback.

name: Plugin compatibility gate with risk-acknowledged per-version exemptions
what: Installing a plugin whose declared DSH peer range does not match the running runtime is refused before pnpm runs, so nothing is downloaded and no build script executes; a user can grant an exact package@version and runtime-version exemption only after accepting a stated crash and data-loss risk.
how: An install naming packages is checked first (local path via its package.json, registry spec via pnpm lookup of the version the range selects and its peers); git and tarball specs are judged after install and the profile manifest and lockfile are restored; exemptions live in the profile's compatibility.json keyed by exact package@version and exact runtime versions, never inherited by upgrades; setVersionExemption requires acceptRisk=true; the agent tool and the CLI (version-exemptions, allow-version --accept-risk, revoke-version) print the risk warning; the service checks the acknowledgement flag, not conversation history.
verevonRelevance: Verevon plugins currently have no install or marketplace surface; when one is built, a pre-install compatibility check plus an explicit, audited override is the safe pattern, with the acknowledgement verified server-side.
notes: Grants take effect on the next composition: a live profile recomposes and reports applied, a startup-only profile reports restart-required.

name: Dependency build-script approvals persisted per package name
what: When pnpm blocks a plugin dependency's install scripts, the failed install lists every pending package and the Web page offers Allow these scripts and retry showing the exact names and the persistent scope; closing the page grants nothing, and an agent may grant only after the user approves in conversation.
how: The manager reports pendingBuilds (including names from earlier attempts) and records them itself because pnpm writes entries only when it can prompt; approval persists by package name in the profile's pnpm-workspace.yaml allowBuilds, permits commands with the host user's permissions, only applies to currently undecided names (denials and wildcard rules cannot be overridden) and rejects YAML anchors or aliases; the install_bundle tool takes approvedBuilds; the service validates names but does not verify that conversation approval occurred.
verevonRelevance: Relevant to any future Verevon plugin or MCP installer that executes third-party code; persisting named approvals and requiring a server-side approval token closes the gap DSH leaves open.
notes: The record states plainly that the service cannot verify the agent's claim of user approval, a limit Verevon should close with a server-side approval token.

name: Structured agent todo list with whole-list replacement and a single owner
what: The agent keeps a visible task list (content plus pending, in-progress or completed status) that survives turns and reopened sessions; each update replaces the whole list, only the owning agent session can change it, and one flag decides whether several tasks may be in progress.
how: dsh-tool-todo mounted in the base bundle with allowParallelInProgress true; ui-tool ships a todo presentation card; the Web bundle disables the base row and exposes the tool through agent presets; no partial updates, no read-back tool, no stable ids or priorities; subagent and shared scopes are deliberately cut.
verevonRelevance: A visible, durable plan list is a baseline agent-page feature; whole-list replacement is simple but costs tokens on long lists, which Verevon could avoid with patch operations.
notes: Deliberately minimal item shape; no subagent or swarm sharing.
